1	# AgentCenter
2	
3	Internal-flavored marketplace for AI agent extensions: Skills, MCP servers, slash commands, plugins. Bilingual (EN/ZH) from day one. See `docs/plan.md` for the full implementation plan and milestone schedule.
4	
5	## Tech stack
6	
7	- TypeScript, Next.js 16 (App Router, RSC, Turbopack dev), Tailwind CSS v4, shadcn/ui + Radix
8	  - Next 16 has breaking changes from earlier versions; consult `node_modules/next/dist/docs/` and the project's top-level `AGENTS.md` before writing Next-specific code.
9	- Bun for local dev and CLI build; Vercel + Node runtime for the web app in prod
10	- PostgreSQL (Neon hosted) with Drizzle ORM
11	- Better Auth (cookie sessions, Drizzle adapter)
12	- Cloudflare R2 for bundle storage
13	- Inngest for background jobs (scan, index, publish)
14	- next-intl for i18n; locales `en` (default) + `zh`, always-prefixed URLs (`/en/...`, `/zh/...`)
15	- Fonts via `next/font`: Inter (UI), Fraunces (display, italic), JetBrains Mono (tags/counts)
16	- Postgres FTS + `pg_trgm` for search; Meilisearch deferred
17	
18	## Locked product decisions
19	
20	1. **Multi-tenant schema, single-tenant UI** for v1.
21	2. **Themes**: Editorial Ivory (default) + Dark. Mono Clean dropped.
22	3. **Filter UI**: Mode B (drawer-style multi-row) only. Modes A/C in the prototype were comparison scaffolding.
23	4. **Sign-up**: open. SSO/invite-only later if needed.
24	5. **Locale URLs**: always prefixed; no implicit default.
25	6. **Detail page README**: raw markdown stored, server-rendered with `react-markdown` + `rehype-sanitize`. Manifest metadata (homepage, repo, license, compatibility, screenshots) rendered as a side panel.
26	7. **Install button**: triggers real install via the Agent CLI. Web records install events; the CLI does the work.
27	8. **Agent CLI**: agent-agnostic with Claude-first defaults. Extensions declare destination paths per agent in their manifest; user can override via `agentcenter config set`. Default target: `~/.claude/...`. Distributed via npm (Bun-built binary).
28	9. **Department IDs**: dotted-path text PKs (e.g. `eng.cloud.infra`). Descendant filter is a single `LIKE 'parent.%'` predicate, not a recursive CTE.
29	10. **Dynamic content i18n**: column-per-language (`name` + `nameZh`, `description` + `descriptionZh`). `tags` table carries `labelEn` + `labelZh`.
30	
31	## Workflow
32	
33	- **Commit per coherent unit** — roughly one per phase, split when natural. Conventional-commits style with phase scope: `feat(p2-db): drizzle schema + seed data`.
34	- Before each commit, surface a diff summary and proposed commit message. Wait for explicit go-ahead before running `git commit`.
35	- At the end of each phase, pause for an explicit checkpoint before starting the next phase.
36	- No `--amend`, no force-push, no `--no-verify`. Corrective commits over history rewrites.
37	- Always work on a feature branch and open a PR — never commit to `main` directly. CI (lint, typecheck, tests) and CodeRabbit run on every PR.
38	- When a binding decision changes, update `docs/plan.md` in the same commit as the code change.
39	
40	## Project structure (target)
41	
42	See `docs/plan.md` §1 for the full tree. High-level layout:
43	
44	- `app/[locale]/...` — App Router pages, locale-segmented
45	- `app/api/...` — Better Auth handler, R2 presigned upload, install events, Inngest webhook, public registry API (`/api/v1/...`) used by the CLI
46	- `components/{ui,layout,extension,filters,publish}` — UI components
47	- `lib/{db,auth,i18n,storage,jobs,search,validators}` — server-side infra
48	- `cli/` — separate Bun-built binary, ships in Phase 9 (agent-agnostic, Claude-first defaults)
49	- `drizzle/` — generated migrations
50	- `docs/` — plan, ADRs, manifest spec
51	
52	## Design references
53	
54	The original prototype lives outside this repo at `/tmp/agentcenter-design/` (extracted from a Claude Design handoff bundle). Key files:
55	
56	- `agentcenter/project/AgentCenter v2.html` — the primary design (1641 lines, Editorial Ivory aesthetic, Mode B filters)
57	- `agentcenter/chats/chat1.md` — full design conversation, including the iteration history that produced the locked decisions
58	
59	These are reference-only. Production components recreate the design in React/Tailwind, not by copying the prototype's inline styles.
60

1	# AgentCenter
2	
3	A bilingual (EN/ZH) marketplace for AI agent extensions — Skills, MCP servers, slash commands, and plugins. Browse, search, and install extensions through the web UI; install them into your agent runtime through the companion CLI.
4	
5	> Status: under active development. The web app and CLI are functional; the manifest spec, deployment guide, and full implementation plan are tracked under [`docs/`](./docs).
6	
7	## What's in here
8	
9	- **Web app** — browse, filter, and view extension detail pages; publish and manage your own extensions; bilingual UI with always-prefixed locales (`/en/...`, `/zh/...`)
10	- **CLI** — agent-agnostic installer with Claude-first defaults; logs in via device-code flow, installs extensions to `~/.claude/...` (or a path you configure)
11	- **Public registry API** — the `/api/v1/...` surface the CLI talks to
12

15	| Layer | Choice |
16	|---|---|

19	| Styling | Tailwind CSS v4, shadcn/ui, Radix |
20	| Runtime | Bun (local dev, CLI build); Node on Vercel (production) |
21	| Database | PostgreSQL (Neon) + Drizzle ORM |
22	| Auth | Better Auth (cookie sessions, Drizzle adapter) |
23	| Storage | Cloudflare R2 (bundle ZIPs, presigned PUT) |
24	| Background jobs | Inngest (scan, index, publish) |
25	| i18n | next-intl, locales `en` + `zh` |
26	| Search | Postgres FTS + `pg_trgm` |

> AGENT

I've scanned the codebase. Here's an honest read on what you're proposing.

## What you'd be rewriting

This is a fairly mature Next.js 16 app, not a toy:

- **App Router + RSC** heavy use: `app/[locale]/...` pages, server components, server actions (`lib/actions`)
- **Better Auth** with Next.js handler + cookie sessions
- **Drizzle + Neon Postgres**, including FTS/`pg_trgm` search
- **Better Auth, Inngest webhooks, R2 presigned uploads, public `/api/v1/...` registry** (consumed by the CLI binary)
- **next-intl** with always-prefixed `/en|/zh` URLs
- **shadcn/ui + Radix + lucide-react** — all React-only component libraries
- **Tailwind v4**, custom theme system (`lib/theme.ts`)
- Vitest + Playwright + RTL test suites
- A separate Bun-built **CLI** that talks to the web app's API

## My honest take

**The hard parts port cleanly. The easy-looking parts don't.**

What ports almost unchanged:
- Drizzle schema, migrations, search SQL, validators (Zod), R2 storage helpers, Inngest job definitions — all framework-agnostic TypeScript. Move them to `server/` in Nuxt and you're done.
- The CLI is untouched (it only talks to HTTP endpoints).
- API routes map naturally to Nuxt's `server/api/v1/...`.

What's painful:
- **Every component must be rewritten in Vue.** shadcn/ui, Radix, lucide-react, react-markdown — none of these exist in Vue form. `shadcn-vue` exists but isn't 1:1; you'll be re-skinning the entire UI.
- **RSC has no Nuxt equivalent.** Nuxt's data fetching model (`useFetch`/`useAsyncData` + server routes) is different from "server component renders, streams to client." You'll restructure how data flows into pages.
- **Server actions → `server/api/` endpoints + client calls.** Mechanical but touches every form/mutation.
- **Better Auth** has a Nuxt integration but it's less battle-tested than the Next one — expect some friction on session handling.
- **next-intl → `@nuxtjs/i18n`** — different API, different routing config. Locale-prefix behavior should be reproducible.

## What I'd ask before recommending

1. **Why Nuxt?** If it's "I prefer Vue," that's a fine reason — say so and we plan accordingly. If it's a perf/DX concern with Next 16, the rewrite probably won't fix it.
2. **What other stack changes?** You said "maybe changing some other tech stack." Drizzle/Neon/R2/Inngest are all framework-agnostic and worth keeping. The risky swaps are auth and i18n.
3. **Is the CLI's API contract frozen?** If so, the rewrite is much safer — you have a regression target.

My recommendation: **don't start coding yet.** Tell me your motivation and any other stack swaps you're considering, and I'll draft a phased migration plan (probably: scaffold Nuxt → port `lib/` server code → port API routes → port pages bottom-up → swap CLI's base URL last).

Neon may change to Supabase. 3. what do you suggest, we can change or no-change the API, all is ok.

> AGENT

Good context. Here's what I'd recommend, going piece by piece.

## Stack recommendations

| Layer | Current | Suggested for Nuxt | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| UI primitives | shadcn/ui + Radix | **shadcn-vue + Reka UI** | Direct port; same philosophy (copy-paste, not a library); Reka is the Vue Radix port |
| Icons | lucide-react | **lucide-vue-next** | Drop-in |
| Markdown | react-markdown + rehype-sanitize | **markdown-it + DOMPurify** (server-rendered) | Don't reach for Nuxt Content — your markdown lives in Postgres, not files. Nuxt Content is for file-based content collections |
| Forms / validation | Server actions + Zod | **`server/api/` endpoints + vee-validate + Zod** | Keep every Zod validator as-is; vee-validate composes well with Zod schemas |
| Data fetching | RSC | **`useAsyncData` / `useFetch` + `server/api/`** | Don't try to recreate RSC with Vue server components — Nuxt's islands are real but immature. The idiomatic Nuxt pattern (SSR via `useAsyncData`) is plenty fast for a marketplace |
| State | Mostly server-resolved | **Pinia only where needed** | Most pages don't need client state. Auth state via composable |
| Background jobs | Inngest | **Keep Inngest** | Framework-agnostic; mount the webhook at `server/api/inngest.ts` |
| i18n | next-intl | **`@nuxtjs/i18n` with `strategy: 'prefix'`** | Reproduces always-prefixed `/en|/zh` URLs cleanly |

## On the Supabase switch

This is the most consequential decision. My take:

1. **Keep Drizzle, point it at Supabase Postgres.** Supabase is just Postgres — Drizzle works the same. Your FTS + `pg_trgm` migrations port directly. Don't adopt the Supabase JS client for general queries; Drizzle's types are better.

2. **Replace Better Auth with Supabase Auth, via `@nuxtjs/supabase`.** This is where switching to Supabase actually earns its keep. You get `useSupabaseUser()` and `useSupabaseClient()` composables, automatic session handling, and one less moving part. Better Auth's Nuxt story is less mature.

3. **Replace Cloudflare R2 with Supabase Storage.** Same vendor, simpler ops, presigned uploads built in. Unless you have a reason to keep R2 (cost at scale, existing tooling), consolidate.

4. **Use Supabase RLS sparingly.** Tempting trap: pushing authz into Postgres policies. For a marketplace where most reads are public and writes go through `server/api/` (validated), do authz in the API layer like you already do. RLS adds debugging overhead you don't need.

End state: Supabase becomes Postgres + Auth + Storage. Inngest stays. That's a clean shape.

## On the API contract

**Keep `/api/v1/...` exactly as-is.** The CLI is shipped (or about to ship) via npm. Breaking that contract means forcing every user to upgrade. Nothing about Nuxt makes the current routes awkward — they map 1:1 to `server/api/v1/...`. Save API redesign for a real v2 driven by CLI features, not by the rewrite.

The *internal* API (forms, install events, R2 presign) is fair game to redesign idiomatically — those have one consumer.

## What I'd want to know before drafting a plan

1. **Is shadcn-vue's coverage acceptable?** It's ~90% of shadcn/ui but a few components lag. Worth a quick check of your `components/ui/` inventory against shadcn-vue's catalog.
2. **Do you want the rewrite to land in parallel** (run both, cut over) or replace in-place? Affects branching and deploy strategy.
3. **Department-ID dotted-path search, README rendering, publish flow** — anything you actively *dislike* in the current product? A rewrite is the cheapest moment to fix those.

If this stack shape looks right, I can draft a phased migration plan next — scaffold → port `lib/` server code → port API → port pages bottom-up.

17	                                          Inngest ──→ Neon + R2 (background jobs)
18	
19	CLI (Bun-built binary) ──── /api/v1/... (Bearer token via device-code flow)
20	```
21	
22	Web requests hit Vercel; the CLI hits the same Vercel deployment but talks only to the `/api/v1` surface. Bundles flow directly between the browser/CLI and R2 via signed URLs — Vercel never proxies binary content.
23	
24	## Web app layout
25	
26	The App Router tree is locale-segmented. URLs are always prefixed (`/en/...`, `/zh/...`); there is no implicit default.
27	
28	```text
29	app/
30	├── layout.tsx                 # html/body, font loaders, theme cookie
31	├── [locale]/
32	│   ├── layout.tsx             # next-intl provider, AppShell (sidebar + topbar)
33	│   ├── page.tsx               # home (featured + trending)
34	│   ├── extensions/
35	│   │   ├── page.tsx           # browse (filter bar + grid)
36	│   │   ├── error.tsx          # listing route error boundary
37	│   │   └── [slug]/
38	│   │       ├── page.tsx       # detail (hero + tabs + sidebar)
39	│   │       └── error.tsx      # detail route error boundary
40	│   ├── publish/
41	│   │   ├── page.tsx           # dashboard (my extensions, with resume + discard)
42	│   │   ├── new/page.tsx       # upload wizard (new draft)
43	│   │   └── [id]/edit/page.tsx # upload wizard (resume / edit existing draft)
44	│   ├── (auth)/sign-in,sign-up
45	│   └── cli/auth/page.tsx      # device-code authorization UI
46	└── api/                       # see "API surfaces" below
47	```
48	
49	### RSC vs client islands
50	
51	Server components render the static shell, fetch data via Drizzle, and stream HTML. Client components are reserved for interactive bits — filter chips, the install button, the upload wizard, the user menu — and are marked with `"use client"`. The pattern is "server frame, client islands."
52	
53	The filter bar (`components/filters/filter-bar.tsx`) is a server component but composes client islands (`FilterChips`, `SortSelect`, `DeptPicker`, `PublisherPicker`, `CreatorPicker`, `TagDrawer`). Each island calls the typed `useFilters()` hook (`lib/hooks/use-filters.ts`), which exposes a parsed `filters` object and an `update(partial)` setter. Filter state lives in the URL — no global store, no context, and back/forward works. The hook delegates URL parsing/serializing to `parseFilters` / `serializeFilters` in `lib/validators/filters.ts` so the same conventions apply to both server-side reads (in RSCs) and client-side writes.
54	
55	### i18n
56	
57	Locales live under `lib/i18n/messages/{en,zh}.json`. `next-intl` is configured with `localePrefix: "always"`. Static UI strings come from `useTranslations(...)`; bilingual content (extension `name` / `nameZh`, tag labels) is column-per-language in Postgres and resolved at the component level via `tagLabel(...)` / direct field access.
58	
59	### Theme
60	
61	`Editorial Ivory` (default) and `Dark`. The active theme is stored in a cookie (`theme`), read in the root layout, and applied as a `data-theme` attribute. The toggle (`ThemeSwitch`) writes the cookie and triggers `router.refresh()`.
62	
63	## Request flows
64	
65	### Browse
66	
67	```text
68	GET /en/extensions?category=skills&dept=eng.cloud&sort=stars
69	  └─ app/[locale]/extensions/page.tsx (RSC)
70	      ├─ parseFilters(searchParams)
71	      ├─ Promise.all([listExtensions, countFilteredExtensions, getTagsWithCounts])
72	      └─ <FilterBar tags={tags} /> + <ExtGrid items={items} />
73	```
74	
75	`buildExtensionWhere` / `buildExtensionOrder` in `lib/search/query.ts` compose Drizzle SQL clauses from filters; they're pure (no DB call), unit-tested, and shared with `/api/v1/extensions` so web and CLI see the same listing semantics.
76	
77	### Detail
78	
79	```text
80	GET /en/extensions/my-skill
81	  └─ app/[locale]/extensions/[slug]/page.tsx (RSC)
82	      ├─ getExtensionBySlug(slug)                ─► extensions row + tag ids
83	      ├─ Promise.all:
84	      │     ├─ getLatestExtensionVersion(id)     ─► version + bundle size for hero / About
85	      │     ├─ listExtensionVersions(id)         ─► full changelog feed for the Versions tab
86	      │     └─ getRelatedExtensions(id, cat)     ─► top 4 by downloads in the same category
87	      └─ <ExtHero /> + <ExtTabs> + <ExtAboutCard /> + <ExtRelatedList />
88	```
89	
90	The page is a two-column layout: the hero (icon block, title + badge, Install/Save/Share CTA row, four-stat grid) sits above a tab strip, with a sticky sidebar on the right.
91	
92	`<ExtTabs>` is a thin wrapper over `@base-ui/react/tabs`, so keyboard navigation, `aria-controls` wiring, and selected-state styling come from the primitive. Four tabs:
93	
94	- **Overview** — README rendered with `react-markdown` + `rehype-sanitize`, followed by a tag chip strip.
95	- **Setup** — the `agentcenter install <slug>` command in a copyable terminal block, plus a Requirements list derived from `extensions.compatibilityJson`.
96	- **Versions** — flat changelog from `listExtensionVersions` (status `ready` only, ordered by `publishedAt DESC`), with the latest entry tagged "Current".
97	- **Reviews** — empty-state placeholder; the reviews flow isn't wired yet.
98	
99	The sidebar has two cards. `<ExtAboutCard>` renders publisher / version / size / license / updated / scope plus the homepage and repo links — every URL passes through `safeExternalUrl()` (allowlists `http(s):`, drops anything else) before reaching `href`. `<ExtRelatedList>` shows the four related extensions; it returns `null` when empty so an empty card never shows.
100	
101	The share URL on the hero is composed from `process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL` rather than the request `Host` header, since spoofable forwarded headers would let an attacker control what gets copied to clipboard.
102	
103	### Publish
104	
105	The wizard is a 4-step rail layout (`<UploadWizard>` in `components/publish/wizard/`): **Basics → Bundle → Listing → Review**, with a sticky live-preview pane that mirrors the listing card and the derived `manifest.json`. Step 1 (Basics) creates the draft on advance; Steps 2-3 mutate it via `updateDraftExtension`; Step 4 submits.
106	
107	```text
108	Browser                          Vercel                          R2          Inngest
109	   │ Basics → Next                  │                              │             │
110	   ├──── createDraftExtension ────► server action  ──► extensions row (visibility=draft)
111	   │                                │                              │             │
112	   ├──── Bundle: upload .zip ───────│─── presigned PUT URL ───────►│             │
113	   │                                │                              │             │
114	   ├──── attachFile(versionId) ────► server action  ──► files row + extensionVersion
115	   │                                │                              │             │
116	   ├──── Listing/Review edits ─────► updateDraftExtension (sourceMethod, tags, README, …)
117	   │                                │                              │             │
118	   ├──── Review → Publish ─────────► submitForReview ──► sendEvent("extension/scan.requested")
119	   │                                │                              │             │
120	   │                                │                              │  scan-bundle:
121	   │                                │                              │   download from R2,
122	   │                                │                              │   sha-256 checksum,
123	   │                                │                              │   parse manifest.toml,
124	   │                                │                              │   validate schema,
125	   │                                │                              │   recordScanResult →
126	   │                                │                              │    scope=personal:
127	   │                                │                              │      version.status=ready
128	   │                                │                              │      + version.publishedAt=now
129	   │                                │                              │      + extensions.visibility=published
130	   │                                │                              │      + extensions.publishedAt=now
131	   │                                │                              │    scope=org|enterprise:
132	   │                                │                              │      version.status=ready
133	   │                                │                              │      (visibility stays draft —
134	   │                                │                              │       awaits admin publishVersion)
135	   │                                │                              │   sendEvent("extension/index.requested")
136	   │                                │                              │             │
137	   │                                │                              │  reindex-search:
138	   │                                │                              │   revalidateTag("extensions")
139	```
140	
141	The upload goes browser → R2 directly (presigned PUT) — Vercel only signs the URL. The Inngest webhook lives at `/api/inngest`. Job source: `lib/jobs/scan-bundle.ts` and `lib/jobs/reindex-search.ts`.
142	
143	A note on `scan-bundle`: download + checksum + manifest parsing live in a single `step.run` rather than separate steps, because Inngest serializes step return values across boundaries and `Buffer` doesn't survive that round-trip.
144	
145	The form is deliberately slimmer than the bundle TOML it eventually publishes. The wizard collects only what users edit interactively (name, slug, summary, type, scope, tags, dept, README, permissions, icon colour, source method); fields that the bundle's `manifest.toml` still requires (`description`, `funcCat`, `subCat`) get backfilled server-side. `extensions.funcCat`/`subCat` are nullable and `defaultClassification(category)` in `lib/actions/publish.ts` derives sensible defaults (`skills`/`plugins` → `tools/general`, `mcp` → `tools/integrations`, `slash` → `tools/commands`) on `createDraftExtension`. `updateDraftExtension` deliberately never writes those columns so admin curation isn't reverted on a draft re-save. New columns: `extensions.permissions` (jsonb of network/files/runtime/data toggles surfaced on the detail page) and `extension_versions.sourceMethod` / `sourceMeta` (text + jsonb — only `'zip'` is wired today; `'git'` and `'cli'` are reserved for future modes).
146	
147	R2 bundle keys are `bundles/<slug>/<version>/bundle.zip` (`bundleKey()` in `lib/storage/r2.ts`). Two consequences worth knowing: (1) the wizard locks `slug` and `version` on the Basics step the moment a draft has been persisted server-side (i.e. once `extensionId` is set) — `updateDraftExtension` deliberately refuses to write either column, and an unlocked field would silently show edits the server will never persist or, worse, orphan the bundle at the old R2 key after upload; and (2) discarding a draft only deletes DB rows; the R2 object is left for bucket lifecycle to garbage-collect.
148	
149	### Resume, edit, and discard
150	
151	The dashboard at `/[locale]/publish` shows each draft's stage (`Needs bundle upload` / `Ready to submit` / `Awaiting scan` / etc., derived from `extensionVersions.status` + `bundleFileId` via `rowAction()` in `lib/publish/row-action.ts`). Rows whose latest version is `pending` are clickable and link into `/publish/[id]/edit`, which loads the draft via `getDraft()` and mounts the same `<UploadWizard>` in resume mode — Basics fields pre-filled, slug + version locked (because `extensionId` is set), and the initial step derived from whether a bundle is uploaded (no bundle → land on Bundle; bundle present → land on Review). Step transitions through Basics call `updateDraftExtension()` instead of `createDraftExtension()`; the action refuses (`version_not_editable`) once status leaves `pending`. Rejected rows aren't clickable but surface the scan reason inline (extracted from `files.scanReport` via `extractScanReason()` in `lib/publish/scan-report.ts`) so the dashboard isn't a dead end for failed scans.
152	
153	Each draft row also gets a `<DiscardButton>` that calls `discardDraft()` — owner-checked, draft-visibility-only, hard delete (FK cascades clean up versions/tags/files-row links). `getDraft` and `discardDraft` deliberately collapse non-owner into `not_found` so the public action contract can't be used to probe existence.
154	
155	### Version state transitions
156	
157	`lib/extensions/state.ts` owns every transition of `extensionVersions.status`, `files.scanStatus`, and `extensions.visibility`. Three functions:
158	
159	- `submit(versionId)` — moves a version into `scanning`. Idempotent: accepts `pending` *or* `scanning` as the source state, so a retry after a failed `inngest.send` can re-queue the scan instead of getting stuck. Versions in `ready` / `rejected` reject the transition.
160	- `recordScanResult(versionId, fileId, result)` — applies the outcome of a bundle scan in one transaction. Failure (`result.ok === false`) sets `files.scanStatus='flagged' + version.status='rejected'`. Success sets `files.scanStatus='clean' + checksumSha256`, then **branches on the parent extension's `scope`**: `personal` → `version.status='ready'` *plus* `version.publishedAt=now()` *plus* `extensions.visibility='published'` + `extensions.publishedAt=now()`, all in the same transaction (auto-publish path); `org` / `enterprise` → only `version.status='ready'`, leaving visibility as `draft` for a later admin call to `publishVersion`. The function joins extensions to read scope on the way in, so the scan job doesn't need to know the rule.
161	- `publishVersion(versionId)` — admin-curation path for `org` / `enterprise` versions. Flips `extensions.visibility='published'` and stamps both rows with `publishedAt`, returning the `extensionId` for the job's downstream `revalidateTag` and `extension/published` event. Personal-scope versions don't go through here — `recordScanResult` already published them.
162	
163	`extensions.search_vector` is a Postgres `GENERATED ALWAYS ... STORED` column (see `drizzle/0002_fts_search_vector.sql`); no application code writes it. The `reindex-search` job's earlier hand-rolled `to_tsvector` UPDATE was dead — the generated column always reflects the source content.
164	
165	### Install (CLI path)
166	
167	```text
168	agentcenter install my-skill
169	  ├─ GET /api/v1/extensions/my-skill                     metadata (name, version, category)
170	  ├─ GET /api/v1/extensions/my-skill/bundle              302 → signed R2 URL
171	  ├─ fetch(signed-url)                                   ZIP bytes
172	  ├─ unzip + write to ~/.claude/skills/my-skill/         (or configured agent path)
173	  └─ POST /api/v1/installs (Bearer token)                records install event, increments downloadsCount
174	```
175	
176	The web "Install" button takes the same conceptual path but goes through the `installExtension` server action instead of the public API: it bumps the same counters and records the same install event, so leaderboards stay consistent across surfaces.
177	
178	Both surfaces are thin wrappers around `recordInstall` in `lib/installs/record.ts`, which owns: extension lookup (by `id` from the web button or `slug` from the CLI), version resolution (an omitted version means "latest published" — `extension_versions` ordered by `publishedAt DESC` among `status='ready'`), the `installs` row insert, the `installed` collection upsert, and the atomic `downloadsCount` bump — all three writes go through `db.transaction`. Each call records a row, so `downloadsCount` is total install events; the `installed` collection is a separate, idempotent membership concept used by the UI's "Installed" view. Failures throw a typed `InstallError` (`extension_not_found`, `no_published_version`); wrappers translate to their surface (action union or HTTP status).
179	
180	## Error handling
181	
182	Server-component throws are caught by App Router `error.tsx` boundaries layered closest-first. Three boundaries today:
183	
184	- `app/[locale]/extensions/error.tsx` — listing-route boundary. Renders a friendly "couldn't load extensions" empty card with a retry button (calls `reset()`); the locale layout (sidebar + topbar) keeps rendering, so users can navigate away even while the listing is broken.
185	- `app/[locale]/extensions/[slug]/error.tsx` — detail-route boundary. Same pattern, plus a **Back to marketplace** link alongside Retry — users may not want to retry the same broken slug. `notFound()` from `getExtensionBySlug` is intercepted by the framework and routes to `not-found.tsx`, not here.
186	- `app/[locale]/error.tsx` — locale-level catchall for any throw the inner boundaries don't cover.
187	
188	All three render generic copy and surface only `error.digest` (the opaque correlation id) — never `error.message`, since Drizzle's `NeonDbError` and friends embed raw SQL fragments and stack traces that would leak internals to users. Boundary copy lives under `extensions.errorBoundary.*`, `detail.errorBoundary.*`, and `errors.generic.*` in the i18n catalogs.
189	
190	The boundaries are uniform — there's no per-query `try/catch` in the page components. A transient Neon `fetch failed` is treated the same as any other server-side throw.
191	
192	## Authentication
193	
194	Two parallel flows on top of one Better Auth instance:
195	
196	- **Web** — cookie sessions. `signIn.email()` from `authClient` (`better-auth/react`) sets the cookie; subsequent server components read the session via `getSession()`. Client components subscribe via `authClient.useSession()` for reactive updates.
197	- **CLI** — device-code flow on top of Better Auth's `verifications` table.
198	  1. CLI: `POST /api/v1/auth/device/code` → server creates two `verifications` rows (`dc:poll:<deviceCode>` and `dc:user:<userCode>`) and returns the user code.
199	  2. User: opens `/{locale}/cli/auth` in a browser, signs in, enters the user code; the page resolves user code → device code, marks the poll row authorized, and stores a session token in it.
200	  3. CLI: polls `POST /api/v1/auth/device/poll` every 5 s. When the row is authorized, the token is returned once and the row is deleted.
201	  4. CLI persists the token in `~/.config/agentcenter/credentials.json` (mode 0600) and uses it as a `Bearer` for authenticated v1 calls.
202	
203	The token is a Better Auth session token — the same kind a browser cookie carries — so the same `sessions` table backs both flows.
204	
205	## API surfaces
206	
207	| Path | Purpose |
208	|---|---|
209	| `/api/auth/[...all]` | Better Auth — session cookies, sign-in, sign-up, sign-out (web) |
210	| `/api/v1/...` | Public registry API consumed by the CLI ([`api.md`](./api.md)) |
211	| `/api/upload/sign` | Web-internal — issues an R2 presigned PUT URL for the upload wizard |
212	| `/api/inngest` | Webhook — Inngest dispatches `scan-bundle` and `reindex-search` here |
213	
214	Only `/api/v1/*` is treated as a contract; the others are implementation details.
215	
216	## Data flow at a glance
217	
218	```text
219	publish wizard ──→ extensions (draft) ──→ files + extensionVersions ──→ Inngest scan
220	                                                                           │
221	                          extensions (published, search_vector) ←──── reindex-search
222	                                            │
223	                          listExtensions (browse) ── installExtension / install API
224	                                                            │
225	                                                       installs row
226	                                                       collections "installed"
227	                                                       downloadsCount++
228	```
229	
230	Every write that affects what users see in the listing (publish, install) ends with a `revalidateTag` so the next browse render hits fresh data.
231

177	
178	## 3. Drizzle schema
179	
180	All in `lib/db/schema/`. `withTimezone: true, defaultNow()` on every timestamp. Text PKs via `nanoid` for user-facing IDs; numeric PKs in junction tables.
181	
182	```ts
183	// schema/auth.ts — Better Auth shape
184	users: id (text pk), email (unique), emailVerified, name, image, bio,
185	       locale ('en'|'zh' default 'en'), themePreference ('ivory'|'dark'|'system'),
186	       defaultDeptId (fk departments.id, nullable), createdAt, updatedAt
187	sessions, accounts, verifications: per Better Auth spec
188	
189	// schema/org.ts
190	organizations: id, slug (unique), name, nameZh, logoUrl, createdAt
191	departments:
192	  id (text pk, dotted-path e.g. "eng.cloud.infra"),
193	  orgId (fk organizations),
194	  parentId (fk departments.id, self-ref, nullable),
195	  name, nameZh,
196	  pathDepth (int — derived for indexing),
197	  createdAt
198	  // INDEX: btree on id (default, used as text_pattern_ops for LIKE), (orgId, parentId), GIN trgm on name
199	memberships: id, userId, orgId, deptId, role ('viewer'|'publisher'|'admin'), createdAt
200	  // UNIQUE (userId, orgId)
201	
202	// schema/extension.ts
203	extensions:
204	  id (text pk, nanoid),
205	  slug (unique, e.g. 'web-search-pro'),
206	  category ('skills'|'mcp'|'slash'|'plugins'),       // pgEnum
207	  badge ('official'|'popular'|'new' | null),
208	  scope ('personal'|'org'|'enterprise'),             // pgEnum
209	  funcCat ('workTask'|'business'|'tools'),           // pgEnum
210	  subCat (text),                                     // l1 key, validated against taxonomy.ts
211	  l2 (text, nullable),
212	  publisherUserId (fk users.id),
213	  ownerOrgId (fk organizations.id),
214	  deptId (fk departments.id),
215	  iconEmoji (text), iconColor (text),
216	  visibility ('draft'|'published'|'archived'),       // pgEnum, default 'draft'
217	  // i18n columns
218	  name, nameZh, description, descriptionZh, tagline, taglineZh,
219	  // metadata for detail page sidebar
220	  homepageUrl, repoUrl, licenseSpdx, compatibilityJson (jsonb — agent versions),
221	  // denormalized counters
222	  downloadsCount (int default 0),
223	  starsAvg (numeric(2,1) default 0),
224	  ratingsCount (int default 0),
225	  // FTS
226	  searchVector (tsvector, generated column — see §8),
227	  publishedAt, createdAt, updatedAt
228	  // INDEXES:
229	  //   idx_ext_category (category)
230	  //   idx_ext_scope (scope)
231	  //   idx_ext_funcSubL2 (funcCat, subCat, l2)
232	  //   idx_ext_dept_prefix on deptId text_pattern_ops  ← critical: enables descendant lookup via LIKE 'eng.cloud.%'
233	  //   idx_ext_search GIN (searchVector)
234	  //   idx_ext_downloads (downloadsCount DESC) for sort
235	  //   idx_ext_stars (starsAvg DESC) for sort
236	
237	extensionVersions:
238	  id, extensionId (fk), version (semver text), changelog, changelogZh,
239	  manifestJson (jsonb), bundleFileId (fk files.id),
240	  status ('pending'|'scanning'|'ready'|'rejected'), publishedAt, createdAt
241	  // UNIQUE (extensionId, version)
242	
243	files:
244	  id (text pk), extensionVersionId (fk, nullable for orphan uploads),
245	  r2Key (text), size (bigint), checksumSha256, mimeType,
246	  scanStatus ('pending'|'clean'|'flagged'), scanReport (jsonb), createdAt
247	
248	tags:
249	  id (text pk = the key, e.g. 'real-time'),
250	  labelEn, labelZh
251	  // INDEX: GIN trgm on (labelEn, labelZh) for autocomplete
252	
253	extensionTags:
254	  extensionId (fk), tagId (fk),
255	  PRIMARY KEY (extensionId, tagId)
256	  // INDEX (tagId, extensionId) for "find ext by tag"
257	
258	// schema/collection.ts
259	collections:
260	  id, ownerUserId, name, nameZh,
261	  systemKind ('installed'|'saved'|null),  // null for user-created groups
262	  createdAt
263	collectionItems:
264	  collectionId, extensionId, addedAt
265	  PRIMARY KEY (collectionId, extensionId)
266	
267	// schema/activity.ts
268	installs:
269	  id, userId, extensionId, version, source ('cli'|'web'),
270	  installedAt, uninstalledAt (nullable)
271	  // INDEX (userId, extensionId), partial WHERE uninstalledAt IS NULL
272	ratings:
273	  id, userId, extensionId, stars (int 1..5), review (text), createdAt
274	  // UNIQUE (userId, extensionId)
275	viewEvents: (P1) id, userId (nullable), extensionId, ts
276	```
277	
278	**Critical indexing notes:**
279	
280	- Department descendant matching uses the dotted-path id directly: `WHERE deptId = $1 OR deptId LIKE $1 || '.%'`. This requires `text_pattern_ops` on `deptId` to use the index for `LIKE`. No recursive CTE.
281	- Filter combinations: `(funcCat, subCat, l2)` covers drill-down.
282	- Sort indexes are separate (`downloadsCount DESC`, `starsAvg DESC`); Postgres index-scans when filter selectivity is low enough.
283	
284	---
285	
286	## 4. i18n strategy
287	
288	- **Library**: next-intl. Locales `en` (default) | `zh`. **Always-prefixed URLs** (`/en/...`, `/zh/...`). Middleware redirects bare `/` → `/en` based on `Accept-Language`.
289	- **Static UI strings**: `lib/i18n/messages/{en,zh}.json`, namespaced by feature (`Sidebar.browse`, `FilterBar.scope.personal`, `Card.installed`). Reuse the prototype's `T` keys verbatim. Server components: `getTranslations()`. Client components: `useTranslations()`.
290	- **Dynamic content** (extension names, descriptions, dept names, tag labels, changelogs): **column-per-language** (`name` + `nameZh`, `description` + `descriptionZh`). Rationale: only 2 locales planned, prototype already uses this shape, keeps `WHERE` and FTS-per-locale simple. Migrate to a `translations` side-table if a 3rd locale arrives.
291	- **Tag labels**: `tags` table carries `labelEn` + `labelZh`, seeded from prototype's `TAG_LABELS`.
292	- **Locale switcher**: `<Link>` swapping the locale segment; preserves filter searchParams.
293	- **FTS**: separate weighted tsvector concatenating all language variants — see §8.

342	
343	## 6. Auth & access model
344	
345	**Better Auth.** Cookie-based server-side sessions; no JWTs (we hit the DB on every RSC request anyway). Drizzle adapter; auth tables live in `lib/db/schema/auth.ts`.
346	
347	- **Sign-up policy**: open. Email + password for v1; SSO/SAML deferred.
348	- **MVP roles** (on `memberships.role`): `viewer` (browse, install, rate), `publisher` (upload), `admin` (moderate).
349	- **Onboarding step** at `/[locale]/onboard` after first sign-up: pick your department. Required before homepage. Org membership auto-created (single-tenant for v1, but `organizations` table is populated so multi-org flip is just middleware later).
350	- **CLI auth**: device-code OAuth flow. CLI displays a short code → user opens `/[locale]/cli/auth`, signs in if needed, enters code, approves → CLI polls `/api/v1/auth/device/poll` until token issued. Token stored at `~/.config/agentcenter/credentials`.
351	
352	---
353	
354	## 7. Upload pipeline
355	
356	```
357	[Publisher] /publish/new  (4-step rail wizard, client component — redesigned)
358	  Step 1: Basics          (name, slug auto-derived, summary ≤80, type, scope;
359	                            optional ZH translation panel)
360	            → Zod validate → server action createDraftExtension() → returns extensionId
361	            → server defaults backfill funcCat/subCat off `category`
362	  Step 2: Source          (zip / git / cli tabs — only zip wired in v1)
363	                          → POST /api/upload/sign  → R2 presigned PUT
364	                          → browser uploads bundle directly to R2
365	                          → server action attachFile(extensionId, fileId)
366	  Step 3: Listing         (icon colour swatch, tag pill input, dept tree
367	                            dropdown, README markdown, permissions checklist)
368	            → server action updateDraftExtension() persists incremental edits
369	  Step 4: Review          → summary cards w/ Edit jump-to-step, scope-aware
370	                            auto-publish vs. admin-review banner
371	                          → submitForReview(versionId)
372	                          → submit(versionId) flips status to 'scanning'
373	                            (idempotent: pending|scanning → scanning, so a retry
374	                             after a failed inngest.send can re-queue the scan)
375	                          → inngest.send({ name: 'extension/scan.requested', ... })
376	                            (best-effort rollback to 'pending' on send failure)
377	                          → return to /publish dashboard
378	
379	[Publisher] /publish (dashboard)
380	  - Lists my drafts with stage (needs upload / ready to submit / scanning / …).
381	  - Resumable rows (status='pending') link to /publish/[id]/edit → same wizard,
382	    pre-filled, slug+version locked while a bundle is uploaded (they form the
383	    R2 bundle key bundles/<slug>/<version>/bundle.zip).
384	  - Per-row Discard button hard-deletes the draft (FK cascades). R2 bundle
385	    objects are left for bucket lifecycle.
386	
387	[Background, Inngest]
388	  on 'extension/scan.requested':
389	    1. fetch from R2
390	    2. checksum + size guard
391	    3. parse manifest.json against ManifestSchema (Zod)
392	    4. (optional) clamav scan
393	    5. write scanReport to files; on clean → status='ready'
394	       → if extension.scope === 'personal': also set extension.visibility='published'
395	         and stamp publishedAt on both rows (auto-publish path)
396	       → otherwise stay at 'ready' awaiting admin curation (publishVersion)
397	    6. inngest.send({ name: 'extension/index.requested', ... })
398	  on 'extension/index.requested':
399	    1. UPDATE extensions SET searchVector = ...
400	    2. flip visibility='published' if all checks pass
401	    3. revalidateTag('extensions')
402	    4. inngest.send({ name: 'extension/published', ... })  // for downstream notifications later
403	```
404	
405	**Synchronous** (server action, returns < 200ms): manifest creation, presigned URL signing, attach-file, submitForReview enqueue.
406	**Async** (Inngest): bundle download, scan, validation, indexing, publish flip.
407	
408	The manifest spec lives in `docs/manifest-spec.md` (drafted in Phase 8 before the wizard). Includes:
409	- Identity: `slug`, `name`, `nameZh`, `version` (semver), `category`, `license`
410	- Discoverability: `tags`, `funcCat`, `subCat`, `l2`, `scope`
411	- Content: `description`, `descriptionZh`, `readme.md`, `screenshots/`
412	- Compatibility: `requires.agent` (e.g. `claude>=0.8`), `requires.os`
413	- Install targets: per-agent destination paths, defaulting to Claude paths
414

416	
417	## 8. Search
418	
419	Postgres FTS with `pg_trgm` fallback for short fuzzy queries.
420	
421	```sql
422	CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS pg_trgm;
423	
424	ALTER TABLE extensions ADD COLUMN search_vector tsvector
425	  GENERATED ALWAYS AS (
426	    setweight(to_tsvector('simple', coalesce(name, '')),       'A') ||
427	    setweight(to_tsvector('simple', coalesce(name_zh, '')),    'A') ||
428	    setweight(to_tsvector('simple', coalesce(tagline, '')),    'B') ||
429	    setweight(to_tsvector('simple', coalesce(tagline_zh, '')), 'B') ||
430	    setweight(to_tsvector('simple', coalesce(description, '')),    'C') ||
431	    setweight(to_tsvector('simple', coalesce(description_zh, '')), 'C')
432	  ) STORED;
433	
434	CREATE INDEX idx_ext_search ON extensions USING GIN (search_vector);
435	CREATE INDEX idx_ext_name_trgm ON extensions USING GIN (lower(name) gin_trgm_ops);
436	CREATE INDEX idx_ext_name_zh_trgm ON extensions USING GIN (name_zh gin_trgm_ops);
437	```
438	
439	**Why `'simple'` config**: Postgres has no built-in zh tokenizer; `zhparser` is an extension Neon may not enable. `'simple'` does whitespace+lowercase only — fine for short marketplace names/taglines in EN, and combined with `pg_trgm` on the same columns gives substring matching for ZH. We can swap the EN side to `'english'` for stemming if/when it matters.
440	
441	**Filter composition** lives in `lib/search/query.ts` as one central `buildExtensionFilters(filters: Filters)` returning a Drizzle `SQL` expression. Filters originate as searchParams, parsed by Zod (`lib/validators/filters.ts`) — so the URL is the filter state (shareable, server-rendered, deeplinkable).
442	
443	```ts
444	const whereClauses = [
445	  eq(extensions.visibility, 'published'),
446	  filters.category && filters.category !== 'all' ? eq(extensions.category, filters.category) : undefined,
447	  filters.scope    && filters.scope !== 'all'    ? eq(extensions.scope, filters.scope) : undefined,
448	  filters.funcCat  ? eq(extensions.funcCat, filters.funcCat) : undefined,
449	  filters.subCat   ? eq(extensions.subCat,  filters.subCat)  : undefined,
450	  filters.deptId   && filters.deptId !== '__all'
451	    ? or(eq(extensions.deptId, filters.deptId), like(extensions.deptId, filters.deptId+'.%'))
452	    : undefined,
453	  filters.q        ? or(
454	                      sql`${extensions.searchVector} @@ websearch_to_tsquery('simple', ${filters.q})`,
455	                      ilike(extensions.name, `%${filters.q}%`),
456	                      ilike(extensions.nameZh, `%${filters.q}%`),
457	                    ) : undefined,
458	  filters.tags?.length
459	    ? inArray(extensions.id,
460	        db.select({ id: extensionTags.extensionId })
461	          .from(extensionTags)
462	          .where(inArray(extensionTags.tagId, filters.tags))
463	          .groupBy(extensionTags.extensionId)
464	          .having(filters.tagMatch === 'all'
465	            ? sql`count(*) = ${filters.tags.length}`
466	            : sql`count(*) >= 1`)
467	      )
468	    : undefined,
469	].filter(Boolean);
470	```
471	
472	Reserve **Meilisearch** for when (a) corpus > ~50k extensions, (b) typo-tolerance becomes a real complaint, or (c) facet counts get expensive.
473

475	
476	## 9. CLI design
477	
478	Separate Bun workspace package (`@agentcenter/cli`), distributed via npm (`npm i -g @agentcenter/cli`) and Homebrew (formula in P1). Single binary built with `bun build --compile` for zero-runtime install.
479	
480	### Architecture
481	
482	```
483	cli/src/
484	├── index.ts              # CLI entrypoint (commander)
485	├── api.ts                # registry API client (typed via shared types)
486	├── auth-store.ts         # ~/.config/agentcenter/credentials (mode 0600)
487	├── config-store.ts       # ~/.config/agentcenter/config.toml
488	├── commands/
489	│   ├── login.ts          # device-code flow
490	│   ├── install.ts        # download + dispatch to installer by category
491	│   ├── uninstall.ts
492	│   ├── list.ts           # list installed extensions on this machine
493	│   ├── config.ts         # set/get/list — agent target paths, registry URL
494	│   └── whoami.ts
495	└── installers/
496	    ├── index.ts          # dispatcher
497	    ├── skills.ts         # P0: download → extract to <agent>/skills/<slug>/
498	    ├── mcp.ts            # P1: register in claude_desktop_config.json or equivalent
499	    ├── slash.ts          # P1: drop into <agent>/commands/
500	    └── plugins.ts        # P1: <agent>/plugins/<slug>/ + activation
501	```
502	
503	### Agent-agnostic with Claude-first defaults
504	
505	The CLI doesn't hard-code Claude paths. Instead:
506	
507	1. **Each extension manifest** declares per-agent install destinations:
508	   ```toml
509	   [install.claude]
510	   skills = "~/.claude/skills/{slug}"
511	   commands = "~/.claude/commands/{slug}"
512	   [install.aider]   # other agents can be supported later
513	   ...
514	   ```
515	2. **CLI config** picks an active agent profile (`agentcenter config set agent claude`) and overrides paths if needed (`agentcenter config set install.basePath /custom/path`).
516	3. **Default agent profile**: `claude`. New users get the right behavior without configuration.
517	
518	### Auth
519	
520	Device-code OAuth grant:
521	1. `agentcenter login` → CLI calls `/api/v1/auth/device/code` → gets `{ user_code, verification_uri }`
522	2. CLI prints: "Visit `https://agentcenter.app/en/cli/auth` and enter `XXXX-YYYY`"
523	3. CLI polls `/api/v1/auth/device/poll` every 5s
524	4. User completes flow on web → server links code to user → poll returns token
525	5. Token persisted to `~/.config/agentcenter/credentials` (mode 0600)
526	
527	### Install flow (Skills, P0)
528	
529	```
530	$ agentcenter install web-search-pro
531	1. CLI → GET /api/v1/extensions/web-search-pro             # manifest + version metadata
532	2. CLI → GET /api/v1/extensions/web-search-pro/bundle      # 302 → R2 signed URL
533	3. Download bundle to temp, verify checksum
534	4. Extract to manifest.install.claude.skills (default ~/.claude/skills/web-search-pro/)
535	5. CLI → POST /api/v1/installs                              # record install event
536	6. Print success + next-steps from manifest.postInstall
537	```
538	
539	P0 supports the **skills** category only (simplest install: extract to a directory). P1 adds MCP (config-file mutation), slash commands (file drop), plugins (activation hooks).
540

543	## 10. Milestone order
544	
545	| Phase | Duration | Deliverable |
546	|---|---|---|
547	| **0. Bootstrap** | 0.5d | `bun create next-app` (TS, App Router, no `src/`), Tailwind v4, shadcn init, fonts via next/font, Drizzle + Neon connection, `.env` template, basic CI lint |
548	| **1. Visual shell** | 1.5d | TopBar + Sidebar + ivory + dark theme tokens; theme-switch component; seed `lib/taxonomy.ts` + `lib/tags.ts` from prototype; statically render the home layout pixel-matched to the prototype |
549	| **2. DB + seed** | 1d | All schema files; `drizzle-kit generate` + `migrate`; `scripts/seed.ts` loads 16 prototype extensions, the dept tree, 32 tags, the func taxonomy. Working `select` query in a server component |
550	| **3. Browse + filter (vertical-slice demo)** | 2d | `/[locale]/extensions` with all filters wired through searchParams; ExtCard component; FilterBar Mode B; dept picker popover; sort. Home shows featured banner + first 6 + Browse All. **Anonymous browse works.** ← clickable demo URL by end of this phase |
551	| **4. Detail page** | 1d | `/extensions/[slug]` — react-markdown + rehype-sanitize for README, metadata sidebar (homepage/repo/license/compat), version table, install button (placeholder, wired in Phase 9) |
552	| **5. i18n** | 1d | next-intl wired, en + zh messages from prototype's `T`, locale switcher, middleware, always-prefixed URLs |
553	| **6. Auth** | 1.5d | Better Auth + Drizzle adapter, sign-in/up pages, dept-pick onboarding, `getSession()` helper, protect publish/collection routes |
554	| **7. Collections + Install events** | 1d | Server actions for `installExtension` (records event), `addToCollection`, `createCollection`; system 'installed'/'saved' collections seeded per user on signup |
555	| **8. Public registry API + manifest spec** | 1d | `docs/manifest-spec.md`, `/api/v1/extensions/...` endpoints, signed bundle URLs, install event POST endpoint |
556	| **9. CLI v1 (skills only)** | 3d | Bun workspace, device-code auth (web side: `/[locale]/cli/auth` page + `/api/v1/auth/device/...`), `install`/`list`/`uninstall`/`config`/`whoami`, agent-agnostic install dispatcher with Claude default. Distributed via npm |
557	| **10. Upload wizard** | 2d | 3-step wizard, R2 presigned upload, draft extension creation, manifest Zod validation |
558	| **11. Background jobs** | 1d | Inngest project init, `scan-bundle` + `reindex-search` functions, webhook route, status polling on publisher dashboard |
559	| **12. Search FTS** | 0.5d | tsvector migration, trgm indexes, top-bar search wired to filter query |
560	| **13. Polish** | 1.5d | empty states, `loading.tsx` + `error.tsx`, OG images, accessibility pass, dark-mode polish across all surfaces |
561	
562	**Total: ~18 days** to v1. Clickable demo URL by end of Phase 3 (~3.5 days in).
563	
564	### P1 (post-v1)
565	- CLI installers for MCP / slash commands / plugins
566	- Publisher dashboard (own extensions, install metrics, version diffs)
567	- Admin moderation
568	- Collection sharing
569	- Ratings & reviews UI on detail page
570	- View events + trending calculation
571	- Homebrew distribution for CLI
572	
573	### P2
574	- MDX docs site at `/docs`
575	- SSO / SAML for enterprise sign-up
576	- Multi-tenant UI (org switcher, per-org branding)
577	- Meilisearch swap-in (only if Postgres FTS is hitting limits)
578	
579	---
580	
581	## 11. Locked decisions (the 10 that drove the plan)
582	
583	These were decided in the planning conversation. Update this section in the same commit when any decision changes.
584	
585	1. **Multi-tenant schema, single-tenant UI** — `organizations` table populated, single org for v1, no org switcher in UI. Multi-org flip is middleware-only later.
586	2. **Auth library**: Better Auth.
587	3. **Background jobs**: Inngest.
588	4. **Themes**: Editorial Ivory + Dark only. Mono Clean dropped.
589	5. **Bundle storage**: Cloudflare R2.
590	6. **Install semantics**: real machine-side install via the Agent CLI. Web records install events; CLI does the work. CLI bumped to **P0**.
591	7. **Sign-up policy**: open.
592	8. **Locale URLs**: always-prefixed (`/en/...`, `/zh/...`).
593	9. **Detail page README**: raw markdown stored, rendered server-side with `react-markdown` + `rehype-sanitize`. Manifest metadata rendered as side panel.
594	10. **CLI strategy**: agent-agnostic with Claude-first defaults. Extensions declare per-agent install paths in the manifest; users override via `agentcenter config`.
595	
596	---
597	
598	## 12. Prototype-to-Next mapping (load-bearing)
599	
600	- `T` object in prototype HTML → split into `messages/en.json` + `messages/zh.json`, preserving keys verbatim.
601	- `DEPARTMENTS` constant → seeded into `departments` table; the dotted-path id is **kept verbatim as the primary key**. This is the load-bearing schema decision — it makes descendant filtering a single `LIKE` predicate.
602	- `FUNC_TAXONOMY` → static TS in `lib/taxonomy.ts`, not a DB table. Product-defined, rarely changes.
603	- `TAG_LABELS` → seeded into `tags` table.
604	- `EXTENSIONS` array → `scripts/seed.ts` rows; `dept`/`scope`/`funcCat`/`subCat` map to typed columns.
605	- `MY_DEPT_ID` constant → comes from authenticated user's `defaultDeptId`.
606	- `isDescendant(deptId, ancestorId)` → moves into the SQL query (`OR LIKE 'ancestor.%'`), no client-side recursion.
607	- `FilterAreaB` (Mode B drawer) is the only filter mode to build; A and C were prototype scaffolding.
608	
```

1	# Contributing
2	
3	## Workflow
4	
5	All changes go through a feature branch and a pull request. There is no direct-to-`main` work.
6	
7	```bash
8	git checkout main && git pull
9	git checkout -b <type>/<short-name>     # see "Branch names" below
10	
11	# ... make your changes ...
12	
13	bun run validate                        # lint + typecheck + tests, mirrors CI
14	git push -u origin HEAD
15	gh pr create                            # or open via the GitHub UI
16	```
17	
18	### Branch names
19	
20	Use a short type prefix matching the kind of work, then a hyphenated name:
21	
22	- `feat/<name>` — new feature
23	- `fix/<name>` — bug fix
24	- `refactor/<name>` — refactor without behaviour change
25	- `test/<name>` — test-only changes
26	- `docs/<name>` — documentation only
27	- `chore/<name>` — tooling, dependency bumps, configuration
28	
29	The `<name>` should describe the area, not the ticket — e.g. `fix/sidebar-i18n`, not `fix/issue-42`.
30	
31	### Commits
32	
33	We use [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/). One coherent unit per commit; split when natural. For multi-phase work, scope by phase: `feat(p10-publish): upload wizard`.
34	
35	```text
36	<type>(<scope>): <one-line summary>
37	
38	<optional body — explain why, not what; reference incidents or invariants
39	that wouldn't be obvious from the diff>
40	```
41	
42	Don't:
43	
44	- Use `git commit --amend` once a commit is on a pushed branch.
45	- Force-push (`--force`, `--force-with-lease`).
46	- Skip hooks (`--no-verify`).
47	
48	If you need to undo work after pushing, prefer a corrective commit over rewriting history.
49	
50	### Pull requests
51	
52	The PR title should be a Conventional Commit summary. The body should cover:
53	
54	- **Summary** — what changed, in 1–3 bullets
55	- **Test plan** — what you ran locally / what reviewers should verify
56	
57	For non-trivial changes, also include:
58	
59	- **Why** — motivation, constraints, or what bug/incident this addresses
60	- **Tradeoffs** — alternatives you considered and why this one won
61	
62	CI runs on every push to a PR (`.github/workflows/ci.yml` — lint, typecheck, vitest). [CodeRabbit](https://www.coderabbit.ai) leaves an automated review. Address its findings before merging; "minor" findings can be deferred with a brief reply explaining why.
63	
64	### Local validation
65	
66	Run `bun run validate` before pushing. It runs the same three checks CI runs in the same order:
67	
68	```bash
69	bun run lint
70	bun run typecheck
71	bun run test
72	```
73	
74	E2E tests (`bun run test:e2e`) require a live dev server with a seeded database — run them locally on demand, not on every PR. They run nightly in [`.github/workflows/e2e.yml`](./.github/workflows/e2e.yml).
75	
76	## Project conventions
77	
78	### Locked product decisions
79	
80	A handful of product/architecture decisions are locked for v1 and shouldn't be revisited inside a normal PR. They're listed in [`CLAUDE.md`](./CLAUDE.md#locked-product-decisions). If a PR needs to change one, update `CLAUDE.md` and `docs/plan.md` in the same commit as the code change.
81	
82	### Tests live next to the code
83	
84	- `lib/**/*.test.ts` and `cli/**/*.test.ts` — unit tests, colocated with their source
85	- `components/**/*.test.tsx` — component tests, colocated, run in happy-dom
86	- `tests/e2e/**/*.spec.ts` — Playwright E2E
87	
88	When you add code under `lib/`, `cli/`, or `components/`, add or update its colocated test file. The vitest glob picks them up automatically.
89	
90	### Style
91	
92	- TypeScript strict — no `any` unless there's a specific reason and a comment.
93	- Prefer editing existing files over creating new ones.
94	- No comments unless the *why* is non-obvious. Don't explain what the code does — name things well instead.
95	- Match the project's terse, factual voice in code, commits, and PR descriptions. No marketing language.
96	
97	## Getting help
98	
99	- Architecture and phase plan: [`docs/plan.md`](./docs/plan.md)
100	- Deployment runbook: [`docs/deploy.md`](./docs/deploy.md)
101	- Manifest spec: [`docs/manifest-spec.md`](./docs/manifest-spec.md)
102	- Project rules (also followed by AI agents): [`CLAUDE.md`](./CLAUDE.md)
103	
```

1	# Deployment Guide
2	
3	AgentCenter deploys to **Vercel** (web app) with **Neon** (Postgres), **Cloudflare R2** (bundle storage), and **Inngest** (background jobs).
4	
5	---
6	
7	## Prerequisites
8	
9	| Service | What you need |
10	|---|---|
11	| [Vercel](https://vercel.com) | Account + project connected to this repo |
12	| [Neon](https://neon.tech) | Project + connection string |
13	| [Cloudflare R2](https://dash.cloudflare.com) | Bucket + API token with Object Read & Write |
14	| [Inngest](https://app.inngest.com) | Account + event key + signing key |
15	
16	---
17	
18	## 1. Neon — database setup
19	
20	1. Create a Neon project in the **US East** region (matches Vercel `iad1`).
21	2. Copy the **pooled** connection string from the Neon dashboard (Pooler tab).  
22	   It looks like: `REDACTED`
23	3. Run the initial migrations (once):
24	   ```bash
25	   # From the repo root, with DATABASE_URL set in your shell or .env.local
26	   bun run db:migrate
27	   ```
28	4. Run the FTS migration (once, after `db:migrate`):
29	   ```bash
30	   psql "$DATABASE_URL" < drizzle/0002_fts_search_vector.sql
31	   ```
32	   Or paste the file contents into the **Neon SQL Editor**.
33	5. Seed reference data (optional, loads sample extensions):
34	   ```bash
35	   bun run db:seed
36	   ```
37	
38	---
39	
40	## 2. Cloudflare R2 — bucket + CORS
41	
42	### Create the bucket
43	
44	1. Go to **Cloudflare dashboard → R2 → Create bucket**.
45	2. Name it `agentcenter-bundles` (or update `R2_BUCKET` env var to match).
46	3. Region: automatic (Cloudflare places it closest to users).
47	
48	### Create an API token
49	
50	1. R2 → **Manage R2 API Tokens → Create API Token**.
51	2. Permissions: **Object Read & Write** scoped to the bucket.
52	3. Copy **Access Key ID** and **Secret Access Key**.
53	4. Copy your **Cloudflare Account ID** from the R2 overview page.
54	
55	### Apply CORS rules
56	
57	Run this once after the bucket is created, and again if the production domain changes:
58	
59	```bash
60	R2_ACCOUNT_ID=xxx \
61	R2_ACCESS_KEY_ID=xxx \
62	R2_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY=xxx \
63	R2_BUCKET=agentcenter-bundles \
64	PRODUCTION_URL=https://yourdomain.com \
65	bun run r2:cors
66	```
67	
68	This allows browsers on `localhost:3000`, `*.vercel.app`, and your production domain to `PUT` bundles directly to R2 via presigned URLs.
69	
70	---
71	
72	## 3. Inngest — background jobs
73	
74	1. Create an Inngest account and a new **app**.
75	2. Copy the **Event Key** and **Signing Key** from the app settings.
76	3. After deploying to Vercel, register the webhook URL in the Inngest dashboard:
77	   ```text
78	   https://yourdomain.com/api/inngest
79	   ```
80	   Inngest will verify it by calling the endpoint. The scan-bundle and reindex-search functions will appear as registered functions.
81	
82	---
83	
84	## 4. Vercel — deploy
85	
86	### Connect the repo
87	
88	1. Vercel → **Add New Project** → import this GitHub repo.
89	2. Vercel auto-detects Next.js and reads `vercel.json` — no framework config needed.
90	
91	### Environment variables
92	
93	Set these in **Vercel → Project → Settings → Environment Variables** (Production + Preview):
94	
95	| Variable | Value |
96	|---|---|
97	| `DATABASE_URL` | Neon pooled connection string |
98	| `BETTER_AUTH_URL` | `https://yourdomain.com` |
99	| `BETTER_AUTH_SECRET` | Random 32+ char string (use `openssl rand -base64 32`) |
100	| `NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL` | `https://yourdomain.com` |
101	| `R2_ACCOUNT_ID` | Cloudflare account ID |
102	| `R2_ACCESS_KEY_ID` | R2 API token key |
103	| `R2_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY` | R2 API token secret |
104	| `R2_BUCKET` | `agentcenter-bundles` (or your bucket name) |
105	| `INNGEST_EVENT_KEY` | From Inngest app settings |
106	| `INNGEST_SIGNING_KEY` | From Inngest app settings |
107	
108	For **Preview deployments** use the same values, or point `DATABASE_URL` at a separate Neon branch.
109	
110	### Deploy
111	
112	Push to `main` — Vercel builds automatically. First deploy checklist:
113	
114	- [ ] All env vars set
115	- [ ] `bun run db:migrate` run against Neon
116	- [ ] `drizzle/0002_fts_search_vector.sql` applied to Neon
117	- [ ] R2 CORS rules applied (`bun run r2:cors`)
118	- [ ] Inngest webhook URL registered
119	
120	---
121	
122	## 5. Local development
123	
124	```bash
125	# 1. Install dependencies
126	bun install
127	
128	# 2. Copy and fill in env vars
129	cp .env.local.example .env.local   # or create .env.local manually (see below)
130	
131	# 3. Run migrations
132	bun run db:migrate
133	
134	# 4. Seed sample data (optional)
135	bun run db:seed
136	
137	# 5. Start dev server
138	bun run dev
139	```
140	
141	### Minimum `.env.local` for local dev
142	
143	```bash
144	# Postgres (Neon)
145	DATABASE_URL="postgresql://..."
146	
147	# App URL
148	NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL="http://localhost:3000"
149	BETTER_AUTH_URL="http://localhost:3000"
150	BETTER_AUTH_SECRET=[REDACTED]"
151	```
152	
153	R2 and Inngest env vars are only needed if you're testing the upload wizard or background jobs locally. Without them, upload signing returns 503 and `submitForReview` will fail gracefully.
154	
155	### CLI (local)
156	
157	```bash
158	cd cli
159	bun run dev login        # opens browser device-code flow
160	bun run dev install <slug>
161	bun run dev list
162	```
163	
164	Or build the binary:
165	
166	```bash
167	cd cli
168	bun run build            # produces cli/dist/agentcenter
169	./dist/agentcenter --help
170	```
171	
172	---
173	
174	## Architecture overview
175	
176	```text
177	Browser → Vercel (Next.js)
178	            ├── App Router pages (RSC + client islands)
179	            ├── /api/auth/...          Better Auth
180	            ├── /api/upload/sign       R2 presigned PUT
181	            ├── /api/v1/...            Public registry API (CLI)
182	            └── /api/inngest           Inngest webhook
183	
184	Vercel → Neon (Postgres, pooled via @neondatabase/serverless)
185	Browser → R2 (direct PUT via presigned URL, no Vercel in the loop)
186	Inngest → Neon + R2 (scan-bundle, reindex-search background jobs)
187	CLI → Vercel /api/v1/... (device-code auth, extension install)
188	```
189	
```

1	# Public registry API
2	
3	The `/api/v1/*` surface is the contract between the web app and the CLI (or any third-party tool that wants to talk to AgentCenter). Other API routes (`/api/auth`, `/api/upload/sign`, `/api/inngest`) are implementation details and are not documented here.
4	
5	All paths are relative to the registry base URL — `https://agentcenter.app` in production, or whatever `registry` value is set in the CLI's `~/.config/agentcenter/config.toml`.
6	
7	## Conventions
8	
9	- Content type is JSON unless otherwise noted.
10	- All write endpoints require `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. The token is obtained via the device-code flow ([`POST /auth/device/code`](#post-apiv1authdevicecode)).
11	- Errors return JSON with the shape `{ "error": "<code>", "message": "<human-readable>" }` and a 4xx/5xx status. Common codes: `unauthenticated` (401), `not_found` (404), `invalid_body` (400), `bundle_unavailable` (503), `server_error` (500).
12	- Listing endpoints set `Cache-Control: public, s-maxage=60, stale-while-revalidate=300`.
13	
14	## Authentication — device code flow
15	
16	The CLI is headless. It exchanges a short-lived **device code** (server-side, opaque) for a **user code** (short, human-readable) the user types into the browser. Once the user authorizes, the CLI polls for a session token.
17	
18	### `POST /api/v1/auth/device/code`
19	
20	Start a login. No auth required.
21	
22	**Response**
23	
24	```json
25	{
26	  "deviceCode": "f9b6c63a-…",
27	  "userCode": "ABCD-1234",
28	  "verificationUri": "/cli/auth",
29	  "expiresIn": 600
30	}
31	```
32	
33	The `verificationUri` is a path on the registry; the CLI is expected to combine it with the registry base URL and open it in the user's browser.
34	
35	### `POST /api/v1/auth/device/poll`
36	
37	Poll for authorization. No auth required. The CLI polls every 5 s.
38	
39	**Request**
40	
41	```json
42	{ "deviceCode": "f9b6c63a-…" }
43	```
44	
45	**Response — pending**
46	
47	```json
48	{ "status": "pending" }
49	```
50	
51	**Response — authorized** (returned exactly once; the row is then deleted)
52	
53	```json
54	{ "status": "authorized", "token": "<session-token>" }
55	```
56	
57	**Response — expired or unknown**
58	
59	```json
60	{ "status": "expired" }
61	```
62	
63	The `token` is a Better Auth session token. The CLI stores it in `~/.config/agentcenter/credentials.json` (mode 0600) and sends it as `Authorization: Bearer <token>` on subsequent calls.
64	
65	## Extensions
66	
67	### `GET /api/v1/extensions`
68	
69	List published extensions. No auth required.
70	
71	**Query parameters** (all optional)
72	
73	| Param | Type | Description |
74	|---|---|---|
75	| `q` | string | Free-text search (Postgres FTS + `pg_trgm`) |
76	| `category` | `skills` \| `mcp` \| `slash` \| `plugins` | Filter by extension category |
77	| `scope` | `personal` \| `org` \| `enterprise` | Filter by scope |
78	| `funcCat` | `workTask` \| `business` \| `tools` | Filter by functional category |
79	| `subCat` | string | Filter by L1 subcategory |
80	| `tags` | comma-separated | e.g. `tags=search,api` |
81	| `tagMatch` | `any` \| `all` | Tag match mode (default `any`) |
82	| `filter` | `official` \| `trending` \| `new` | Curated filter |
83	| `sort` | `downloads` \| `stars` \| `recent` | Sort order (default `downloads`) |
84	| `page` | integer ≥ 1 | Page number, page size is fixed at 24 |
85	
86	**Response**
87	
88	```json
89	{
90	  "items": [
91	    {
92	      "slug": "web-search",
93	      "name": "Web Search",
94	      "nameZh": "网页搜索",
95	      "category": "skills",
96	      "scope": "personal",
97	      "badge": "official",
98	      "description": "Search the web from your agent.",
99	      "descriptionZh": "在你的智能体中搜索网页。",
100	      "tags": ["search", "api"],
101	      "funcCat": "workTask",
102	      "subCat": "softDev",
103	      "l2": "frontend",
104	      "downloadsCount": 1248,
105	      "starsAvg": "4.7"
106	    }
107	  ],
108	  "total": 87,
109	  "page": 1,
110	  "pageSize": 24
111	}
112	```
113	
114	### `GET /api/v1/extensions/:slug`
115	
116	Full metadata for a single extension. No auth required.
117	
118	**Response**
119	
120	```json
121	{
122	  "slug": "web-search",
123	  "name": "Web Search",
124	  "nameZh": "网页搜索",
125	  "category": "skills",
126	  "scope": "personal",
127	  "badge": "official",
128	  "tagline": "One-line tagline",
129	  "description": "Longer description.",
130	  "descriptionZh": "更长的描述。",
131	  "tags": ["search", "api"],
132	  "funcCat": "workTask",
133	  "subCat": "softDev",
134	  "l2": "frontend",
135	  "license": "MIT",
136	  "homepageUrl": "https://example.com",
137	  "repoUrl": "https://github.com/example/web-search",
138	  "compatibilityJson": { "agent": "claude", "minVersion": "1.0" },
139	  "downloadsCount": 1248,
140	  "starsAvg": "4.7",
141	  "ratingsCount": 42,
142	  "publishedAt": "2026-01-15T08:30:00.000Z",
143	  "version": "latest",
144	  "bundleUrl": "/api/v1/extensions/web-search/bundle"
145	}
146	```
147	
148	`version` is currently the literal string `"latest"`; full version history is not yet exposed.
149	
150	`bundleUrl` is a relative path to [`GET /api/v1/extensions/:slug/bundle`](#get-apiv1extensionsslugbundle) — clients should resolve it against the registry base URL.
151	
152	**Errors**
153	
154	- `404 not_found` — slug doesn't exist or isn't published.
155	
156	### `GET /api/v1/extensions/:slug/bundle`
157	
158	Download the latest ready bundle. No auth required. Returns a **302 redirect** to a Cloudflare R2 signed URL — clients should follow it (or read the `Location` header if they want to log the URL).
159	
160	**Errors**
161	
162	- `404 not_found` — slug doesn't exist.
163	- `503 bundle_unavailable` — extension exists but no version has reached `ready` status (still scanning, or scan failed).
164	
165	The signed URL is valid for ~5 minutes. Clients should fetch the bundle immediately rather than caching the redirect.
166	
167	## Installs
168	
169	### `POST /api/v1/installs`
170	
171	Record a successful install. **Requires** `Authorization: Bearer <token>`.
172	
173	The CLI calls this *after* it has unzipped the bundle and written files locally — so even if the registry is unreachable at install time, the local install still succeeds.
174	
175	**Request**
176	
177	```json
178	{
179	  "extensionSlug": "web-search",
180	  "version": "1.2.0",
181	  "agentName": "claude",
182	  "agentVersion": "1.0.4"
183	}
184	```
185	
186	`agentName` and `agentVersion` are informational — stored for analytics but not validated against an agent registry.
187	
188	**Response**
189	
190	```json
191	{
192	  "ok": true,
193	  "installId": "9f2d…",
194	  "isFirstInstall": true,
195	  "version": "1.2.0"
196	}
197	```
198	
199	Every call records an `installs` row and bumps `downloadsCount`. `isFirstInstall` is `true` when this user has no prior install record for this extension; subsequent reinstalls and version upgrades return `false`. `version` is the resolved semver — if the request omitted `version` (or sent the legacy `"latest"` sentinel), this is the latest published version at the moment of install.
200	
201	**Errors**
202	
203	- `401 unauthenticated` — missing or invalid Bearer token.
204	- `400 invalid_body` — body failed schema validation.
205	- `404 not_found` — slug doesn't exist.
206	- `422 no_published_version` — slug exists but has no `ready` version yet (only possible when `version` is omitted).
207	- `500 internal_error` — unhandled server error.
208	
209	## Versioning
210	
211	The surface above is `/api/v1`. Breaking changes will introduce `/api/v2/...` — the `v1` namespace will not change incompatibly. Additive changes (new optional fields, new endpoints) may land within `v1` without notice.
212	
```

# AgentCenter Nuxt — Migration Plan

## A. Which existing rules carry over (and how they translate)

### Rules to keep verbatim

| Rule | Source | Why it still applies |
|---|---|---|
| Conventional Commits, phase-scoped (`feat(p2-db): ...`) | CONTRIBUTING | Framework-agnostic |
| Feature branch + PR, no direct-to-main | CONTRIBUTING | Workflow, not tech |
| No `--amend`, no force-push, no `--no-verify` | CLAUDE.md | Safety rules |
| Branch names `feat/<n>`, `fix/<n>`, etc. | CONTRIBUTING | Framework-agnostic |
| Tests colocated (`lib/**/*.test.ts`, component tests next to component) | CONTRIBUTING | Works the same in Nuxt; Vitest already supports `.vue` via `@vue/test-utils` |
| TS strict, no `any` without a reason | CONTRIBUTING | Framework-agnostic |
| No comments unless *why* is non-obvious | CLAUDE.md | Style, framework-agnostic |
| Terse, factual voice in code/commits/PRs | CONTRIBUTING | Style |
| Commit per coherent unit, one per phase, split when natural | CLAUDE.md | Workflow |
| Update `docs/plan.md` in same commit as a decision change | CLAUDE.md | Process |
| All 10 **Locked product decisions** | CLAUDE.md / plan.md §11 | Product, not tech — themes, locale URLs, install-via-CLI, dept dotted-path PKs, column-per-language i18n, etc. |

### Rules to adapt

| Original | Nuxt version |
|---|---|
| `AGENTS.md`: "This is NOT the Next.js you know — read `node_modules/next/dist/docs/`" | Replace with: "This is Nuxt 4 + Nitro. Conventions changed between Nuxt 3 and 4 — read `node_modules/nuxt/docs/` (if available) or the official docs before writing framework code." |
| App Router + RSC + server actions | Nuxt 4 file-based routing + Nitro `server/api/` + `useFetch`/`useAsyncData` |
| "Server frame, client islands" | Becomes "SSR-by-default Vue components; client-only via `<ClientOnly>` or `.client.vue`" |
| `revalidateTag` after writes | Nitro cache invalidation (`defineCachedEventHandler` + cache keys), or `refresh()` on the consuming `useAsyncData` call |
| ESLint config (`eslint.config.mjs`) | Replace `eslint-config-next` with `@nuxt/eslint` |
| `validate` script (lint+typecheck+test) | Same script, same order: `nuxt typecheck` instead of `tsc --noEmit` |
| Playwright config | Keep; point at new dev server URL/port |

### Locked product decisions — re-evaluation

All 10 stay locked. The two that touch infra:

- **#5 R2 for bundle storage** — keep if deploying to Cloudflare (native bindings, no S3 SDK). If switching to Supabase Storage, lock that instead and update `CLAUDE.md` + `docs/plan.md` in the same commit.
- **#3 Background jobs: Inngest** — Inngest works on Cloudflare; the webhook is just an HTTP endpoint. Keep, unless you want to use **Cloudflare Queues** (only viable on the Cloudflare deploy target) or a Postgres-backed worker for local deploys. My recommendation: **keep Inngest** — it's the only choice that works on both Cloudflare and local.

## B. Target tech stack

| Layer | Choice | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Framework | **Nuxt 4** (Nitro server, Vue 3, Vite) | `compatibilityVersion: 4` |
| Language | TypeScript strict | Same |
| UI primitives | **shadcn-vue** (Reka UI under the hood) | Direct port of shadcn/ui philosophy |
| Icons | **lucide-vue-next** | Drop-in |
| Styling | **Tailwind v4** via `@nuxtjs/tailwindcss` or `@tailwindcss/vite` | Theme tokens unchanged |
| Fonts | **`@nuxt/fonts`** | Inter / Fraunces / JetBrains Mono — same set |
| i18n | **`@nuxtjs/i18n`** with `strategy: 'prefix'` | Always-prefixed `/en`, `/zh` |
| State (where needed) | **Pinia** via `@pinia/nuxt` | Mostly server-resolved; Pinia only for cross-component client state |
| Forms / validation | **vee-validate + @vee-validate/zod** + existing Zod schemas | Keeps every validator |
| Markdown | **markdown-it + DOMPurify** server-side | Replaces `react-markdown` + `rehype-sanitize` |
| Database | **Postgres** via **Drizzle ORM** | Unchanged; works against Neon, Supabase, or self-hosted |
| Hosting target | **Supabase** (recommended) | Postgres + Auth + Storage |
| Auth | **`@nuxtjs/supabase`** (if Supabase) **or** Better Auth via community Nuxt integration | Recommend Supabase Auth — consolidates infra |
| Storage | **Supabase Storage** (if Supabase) **or** **R2** (if Cloudflare-native) | One or the other, not both |
| Background jobs | **Inngest** | Mount at `server/api/inngest.post.ts` |
| Search | **Postgres FTS + `pg_trgm`** | Unchanged SQL |
| Tests | **Vitest** (`@nuxt/test-utils`) + **Playwright** | Same suites |
| Lint | **`@nuxt/eslint`** | Replaces `eslint-config-next` |
