1	import { db } from "@/lib/db/client";
2	import { verifications } from "@/lib/db/schema/auth";
3	import { jsonError } from "@/lib/api/auth";
4	
5	export const runtime = "nodejs";
6	
7	const EXPIRY_MS = 10 * 60 * 1000; // 10 minutes
8	
9	function generateUserCode(): string {
10	  const chars = "REDACTED";
11	  const part = () =>
12	    Array.from(
13	      { length: 4 },
14	      () => chars[Math.floor(Math.random() * chars.length)],
15	    ).join("");
16	  return `${part()}-${part()}`;
17	}
18	
19	// POST /api/v1/auth/device/code
20	// Called by CLI at the start of the login flow. No auth required.
21	export async function POST() {
22	  const deviceCode = crypto.randomUUID();
23	  const userCode = generateUserCode();
24	  const expiresAt = new Date(Date.now() + EXPIRY_MS);
25	
26	  try {
27	    // Poll record — CLI queries by deviceCode.
28	    await db.insert(verifications).values({
29	      id: crypto.randomUUID(),
30	      identifier: `dc:poll:${deviceCode}`,
31	      value: JSON.stringify({ userCode, authorized: false, token: null, userId: null }),
32	      expiresAt,
33	    });
34	
35	    // Reverse-lookup — web page queries by userCode.
36	    await db.insert(verifications).values({
37	      id: crypto.randomUUID(),
38	      identifier: `dc:user:${userCode}`,
39	      value: deviceCode,
40	      expiresAt,
41	    });
42	  } catch {
43	    return jsonError("Failed to create device code.", 500, "server_error");
44	  }
45	
46	  return Response.json({
47	    deviceCode,
48	    userCode,
49	    verificationUri: "/cli/auth",
50	    expiresIn: EXPIRY_MS / 1000,
51	  });
52	}

1	import { and, eq, gt } from "drizzle-orm";
2	import { z } from "zod/v4";
3	
4	import { jsonError } from "@/lib/api/auth";
5	import { db } from "@/lib/db/client";
6	import { verifications } from "@/lib/db/schema/auth";
7	
8	export const runtime = "nodejs";
9	
10	const PollBody = z.object({ deviceCode: z.string().uuid() });
11	
12	// POST /api/v1/auth/device/poll
13	// CLI calls this every 5 s. Returns pending / authorized (+ token) / expired.
14	export async function POST(req: Request) {
15	  let body: z.infer<typeof PollBody>;
16	  try {
17	    body = PollBody.parse(await req.json());
18	  } catch {
19	    return jsonError("Invalid request body.", 400, "invalid_body");
20	  }
21	
22	  const [row] = await db
23	    .select({ id: verifications.id, value: verifications.value })
24	    .from(verifications)
25	    .where(
26	      and(
27	        eq(verifications.identifier, `dc:poll:${body.deviceCode}`),
28	        gt(verifications.expiresAt, new Date()),
29	      ),
30	    )
31	    .limit(1);
32	
33	  if (!row) return Response.json({ status: "expired" });
34	
35	  const state = JSON.parse(row.value) as {
36	    authorized: boolean;
37	    token: string | null;
38	  };
39	
40	  if (!state.authorized) return Response.json({ status: "pending" });
41	
42	  // Clean up after handing out the token once.
43	  await db.delete(verifications).where(eq(verifications.id, row.id));
44	
45	  return Response.json({ status: "authorized", token: state.token });
46	}
47

6	export async function getOrCreateSystemCollection(
7	  userId: string,

10	  const existing = await db
11	    .select({ id: collections.id })
12	    .from(collections)
13	    .where(

24	    name: kind === "installed" ? "Installed" : "Saved",

1	import { S3Client, PutObjectCommand } from "@aws-sdk/client-s3";
2	import { getSignedUrl } from "@aws-sdk/s3-request-presigner";
3	
4	const R2_BUCKET = process.env.R2_BUCKET ?? "agentcenter-bundles";
5	
6	// Validated on first use rather than at import time, so unrelated tests /
7	// build steps that import this module without ever calling presign don't
8	// blow up on missing creds.
9	function getR2Config(): {
10	  accountId: string;
11	  accessKeyId: string;
12	  secretAccessKey: string;
13	} {
14	  const accountId = process.env.R2_ACCOUNT_ID;
15	  const accessKeyId = process.env.R2_ACCESS_KEY_ID;
16	  const secretAccessKey = process.env.R2_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY;
17	  const missing = [
18	    !accountId && "R2_ACCOUNT_ID",
19	    !accessKeyId && "R2_ACCESS_KEY_ID",
20	    !secretAccessKey && "R2_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY",
21	  ].filter(Boolean);
22	  if (missing.length > 0) {
23	    // Failing here surfaces a clear message via the upload-sign route's
24	    // catch block instead of an empty-subdomain URL that DNS-fails in the
25	    // browser as `TypeError: Failed to fetch`.
26	    throw new Error(
27	      `R2 is not configured — missing env vars: ${missing.join(", ")}. ` +
28	        `See .env.example.`,
29	    );
30	  }
31	  return {
32	    accountId: accountId as string,
33	    accessKeyId: accessKeyId as string,
34	    secretAccessKey: secretAccessKey as string,
35	  };
36	}
37	
38	function getClient(): S3Client {
39	  const { accountId, accessKeyId, secretAccessKey } = getR2Config();
40	  return new S3Client({
41	    region: "auto",
42	    endpoint: `https://${accountId}.r2.cloudflarestorage.com`,
43	    credentials: { accessKeyId, secretAccessKey },
44	  });
45	}
46	
47	export async function generatePresignedPutUrl(
48	  key: string,
49	  contentType: string,
50	  expiresInSeconds = 300,
51	): Promise<string> {
52	  const client = getClient();
53	  const command = new PutObjectCommand({
54	    Bucket: R2_BUCKET,
55	    Key: key,
56	    ContentType: contentType,
57	  });
58	  return getSignedUrl(client, command, { expiresIn: expiresInSeconds });
59	}
60	
61	export async function generatePresignedGetUrl(
62	  key: string,
63	  expiresInSeconds = 3600,
64	): Promise<string> {
65	  const { GetObjectCommand } = await import("@aws-sdk/client-s3");
66	  const client = getClient();
67	  const command = new GetObjectCommand({ Bucket: R2_BUCKET, Key: key });
68	  return getSignedUrl(client, command, { expiresIn: expiresInSeconds });
69	}
70	
71	export function bundleKey(slug: string, version: string): string {
72	  return `bundles/${slug}/${version}/bundle.zip`;
73	}
74

}

  "content": "import { and, eq, gt } from \"drizzle-orm\"\nimport { z } from \"zod\"\nimport { verifications } from \"~~/shared/db/schema/auth\"\n\nconst PollBody = z.object({ deviceCode: z.string().uuid() })\n\nexport default defineEventHandler(async (event) => {\n  let body: z.infer<typeof PollBody>\n  try {\n    body = PollBody.parse(await readBody(event))\n  } catch {\n    apiError(event, \"Invalid request body.\", 400, \"invalid_body\")\n  }\n\n  const db = useDb()\n  const [row] = await db\n    .select({ id: verifications.id, value: verifications.value })\n    .from(verifications)\n    .where(\n      and(\n        eq(verifications.identifier, `dc:poll:${body.deviceCode}`),\n        gt(verifications.expiresAt, new Date()),\n      ),\n    )\n    .limit(1)\n\n  if (!row) return { status: \"expired\" }\n\n  const state = JSON.parse(row.value) as { authorized: boolean; token: string | null }\n  if (!state.authorized) return { status: \"pending\" }\n\n  await db.delete(verifications).where(eq(verifications.id, row.id))\n  return { status: \"authorized\", token: state.token }\n})\n"
}

5	import { getSession } from "@/lib/auth/session";
6	import { db } from "@/lib/db/client";
7	import { sessions, verifications } from "@/lib/db/schema/auth";
8	
9	export type AuthorizeResult =
10	  | { ok: true }
11	  | { ok: false; error: "unauthenticated" | "invalid_code" | "expired" | "server_error" };
12	
13	export async function authorizeDevice(userCode: string): Promise<AuthorizeResult> {
14	  const session = await getSession();
15	  if (!session) return { ok: false, error: "unauthenticated" };
16	
17	  const now = new Date();
18	
19	  // Look up the reverse-lookup record to get the deviceCode.
20	  const [lookup] = await db
21	    .select({ id: verifications.id, value: verifications.value })
22	    .from(verifications)
23	    .where(
24	      and(
25	        eq(verifications.identifier, `dc:user:${userCode.toUpperCase()}`),
26	        gt(verifications.expiresAt, now),
27	      ),
28	    )
29	    .limit(1);
30	
31	  if (!lookup) return { ok: false, error: "invalid_code" };
32	
33	  const deviceCode = lookup.value;
34	
35	  // Find the poll record and update it with an authorized CLI session token.
36	  const [pollRow] = await db
37	    .select({ id: verifications.id })
38	    .from(verifications)
39	    .where(
40	      and(
41	        eq(verifications.identifier, `dc:poll:${deviceCode}`),
42	        gt(verifications.expiresAt, now),
43	      ),
44	    )
45	    .limit(1);
46	
47	  if (!pollRow) return { ok: false, error: "expired" };
48	
49	  // Create a long-lived CLI session (30 days).
50	  const cliToken = crypto.randomUUID();
51	  const expiresAt = new Date(Date.now() + 30 * 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000);
52	
53	  await db.insert(sessions).values({
54	    id: crypto.randomUUID(),
55	    userId: session.user.id,
56	    token: cliToken,
57	    expiresAt,
58	  });
59	
60	  // Stamp the poll record as authorized.
61	  await db
62	    .update(verifications)
63	    .set({
64	      value: JSON.stringify({
65	        authorized: true,
66	        token: cliToken,
67	        userId: session.user.id,
68	      }),
69	    })
70	    .where(eq(verifications.id, pollRow.id));
71	
72	  // Clean up the reverse-lookup record.
73	  await db.delete(verifications).where(eq(verifications.id, lookup.id));
74	
75	  return { ok: true };
76	}
77

{
  "file_path": "/Users/hutusi/workspace/ai/naive/agentcenter-nuxt/server/api/internal/device-authorize.post.ts",
  "content": "import { and, eq, gt } from \"drizzle-orm\"\nimport { z } from \"zod\"\nimport { sessions, verifications } from \"~~/shared/db/schema/auth\"\n\nconst bodySchema = z.object({\n  userCode: z.string().trim().min(1).max(20),\n})\n\nexport default defineEventHandler(async (event) => {\n  const user = await requireUser(event)\n  const body = await readValidatedBody(event, (raw) => bodySchema.parse(raw))\n  const userCode = body.userCode.toUpperCase()\n\n  const db = useDb()\n  const now = new Date()\n\n  const [lookup] = await db\n    .select({ id: verifications.id, value: verifications.value })\n    .from(verifications)\n    .where(\n      and(\n        eq(verifications.identifier, `dc:user:${userCode}`),\n        gt(verifications.expiresAt, now),\n      ),\n    )\n    .limit(1)\n\n  if (!lookup) return { ok: false, error: \"invalid_code\" as const }\n\n  const deviceCode = lookup.value\n  const [pollRow] = await db\n    .select({ id: verifications.id })\n    .from(verifications)\n    .where(\n      and(\n        eq(verifications.identifier, `dc:poll:${deviceCode}`),\n        gt(verifications.expiresAt, now),\n      ),\n    )\n    .limit(1)\n\n  if (!pollRow) return { ok: false, error: \"expired\" as const }\n\n  const cliToken = crypto.randomUUID()\n  const expiresAt = new Date(Date.now() + 30 * 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000)\n\n  await db.insert(sessions).values({\n    id: crypto.randomUUID(),\n    userId: user.id,\n    token: cliToken,\n    expiresAt,\n  })\n\n  await db\n    .update(verifications)\n    .set({\n      value: JSON.stringify({\n        authorized: true,\n        token: cliToken,\n        userId: user.id,\n      }),\n    })\n    .where(eq(verifications.id, pollRow.id))\n\n  await db.delete(verifications).where(eq(verifications.id, lookup.id))\n\n  return { ok: true as const }\n})\n"
}

{
  "file_path": "/Users/hutusi/workspace/ai/naive/agentcenter-nuxt/server/utils/storage.ts",
  "content": "// Pluggable storage backend. Supabase Storage is the default (locked decision);\n// R2 via S3 SDK is activated when R2_ACCOUNT_ID is set instead of SUPABASE_URL.\n\ninterface StorageBackend {\n  bundleKey(slug: string, version: string): string\n  getSignedUploadUrl(key: string, contentType: string, expiresInSeconds?: number): Promise<string>\n  getSignedDownloadUrl(key: string, expiresInSeconds?: number): Promise<string>\n}\n\nexport function bundleKey(slug: string, version: string): string {\n  return `bundles/${slug}/${version}/bundle.zip`\n}\n\nlet _backend: StorageBackend | undefined\n\nasync function makeBackend(): Promise<StorageBackend> {\n  if (process.env.R2_ACCOUNT_ID) return makeR2Backend()\n  if (process.env.SUPABASE_URL) return makeSupabaseBackend()\n  throw new Error(\n    \"Storage is not configured — set either SUPABASE_URL (+ SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY + SUPABASE_BUCKET) \" +\n      \"or R2_ACCOUNT_ID (+ R2_ACCESS_KEY_ID + R2_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY + R2_BUCKET). See .env.example.\",\n  )\n}\n\nexport async function useStorage(): Promise<StorageBackend> {\n  if (!_backend) _backend = await makeBackend()\n  return _backend\n}\n\nasync function makeSupabaseBackend(): Promise<StorageBackend> {\n  const url = requireEnv(\"SUPABASE_URL\")\n  const key = requireEnv(\"SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY\")\n  const bucket = process.env.SUPABASE_BUCKET ?? \"agentcenter-bundles\"\n  const { createClient } = await import(\"@supabase/supabase-js\")\n  const client = createClient(url, key, { auth: { persistSession: false } })\n\n  return {\n    bundleKey,\n    async getSignedUploadUrl(objectKey, _contentType, expiresInSeconds = 300) {\n      const { data, error } = await client.storage\n        .from(bucket)\n        .createSignedUploadUrl(objectKey, { upsert: true })\n      if (error || !data) throw error ?? new Error(\"Failed to create signed upload URL\")\n      void expiresInSeconds\n      return data.signedUrl\n    },\n    async getSignedDownloadUrl(objectKey, expiresInSeconds = 3600) {\n      const { data, error } = await client.storage\n        .from(bucket)\n        .createSignedUrl(objectKey, expiresInSeconds)\n      if (error || !data) throw error ?? new Error(\"Failed to create signed download URL\")\n      return data.signedUrl\n    },\n  }\n}\n\nasync function makeR2Backend(): Promise<StorageBackend> {\n  const accountId = requireEnv(\"R2_ACCOUNT_ID\")\n  const accessKeyId = requireEnv(\"R2_ACCESS_KEY_ID\")\n  const secretAccessKey = requireEnv(\"R2_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY\")\n  const bucket = process.env.R2_BUCKET ?? \"agentcenter-bundles\"\n  const { S3Client, PutObjectCommand, GetObjectCommand } = await import(\"@aws-sdk/client-s3\")\n  const { getSignedUrl } = await import(\"@aws-sdk/s3-request-presigner\")\n\n  const client = new S3Client({\n    region: \"auto\",\n    endpoint: `https://${accountId}.r2.cloudflarestorage.com`,\n    credentials: { accessKeyId, secretAccessKey },\n  })\n\n  return {\n    bundleKey,\n    async getSignedUploadUrl(objectKey, contentType, expiresInSeconds = 300) {\n      const command = new PutObjectCommand({\n        Bucket: bucket,\n        Key: objectKey,\n        ContentType: contentType,\n      })\n      return getSignedUrl(client, command, { expiresIn: expiresInSeconds })\n    },\n    async getSignedDownloadUrl(objectKey, expiresInSeconds = 3600) {\n      const command = new GetObjectCommand({ Bucket: bucket, Key: objectKey })\n      return getSignedUrl(client, command, { expiresIn: expiresInSeconds })\n    },\n  }\n}\n\nfunction requireEnv(name: string): string {\n  const value = process.env[name]\n  if (!value) throw new Error(`Missing ${name} env var. See .env.example.`)\n  return value\n}\n"
}

  "content": "import { z } from \"zod\"\n\nconst bodySchema = z.object({\n  slug: z.string().trim().min(1).max(120),\n  version: z.string().trim().min(1).max(60),\n  contentType: z.string().trim().min(1).max(120).default(\"application/zip\"),\n})\n\nexport default defineEventHandler(async (event) => {\n  await requireUser(event)\n  const body = await readValidatedBody(event, (raw) => bodySchema.parse(raw))\n\n  try {\n    const storage = await useStorage()\n    const key = storage.bundleKey(body.slug, body.version)\n    const url = await storage.getSignedUploadUrl(key, body.contentType)\n    return { url, key }\n  } catch (err) {\n    console.error(\"[upload/sign] storage error:\", err)\n    apiError(event, \"Storage is not configured.\", 503, \"storage_unavailable\")\n  }\n})\n"
}

  "content": "import { eq } from \"drizzle-orm\"\nimport {\n  extensions,\n  extensionVersions,\n  files,\n} from \"~~/shared/db/schema\"\nimport { getExtensionBySlug } from \"~~/server/utils/queries/extension-detail\"\n\nexport default defineEventHandler(async (event) => {\n  const slug = getRouterParam(event, \"slug\")\n  if (!slug) apiError(event, \"slug required\", 400, \"invalid_request\")\n\n  const ext = await getExtensionBySlug(slug)\n  if (!ext) apiError(event, \"Extension not found.\", 404, \"not_found\")\n\n  const db = useDb()\n  const [row] = await db\n    .select({ r2Key: files.r2Key })\n    .from(extensionVersions)\n    .innerJoin(files, eq(files.id, extensionVersions.bundleFileId))\n    .innerJoin(extensions, eq(extensions.id, extensionVersions.extensionId))\n    .where(eq(extensions.slug, slug))\n    .orderBy(extensionVersions.createdAt)\n    .limit(1)\n\n  if (!row?.r2Key) {\n    apiError(event, \"Bundle not available yet.\", 503, \"bundle_unavailable\")\n  }\n\n  try {\n    const storage = await useStorage()\n    const url = await storage.getSignedDownloadUrl(row.r2Key)\n    await sendRedirect(event, url, 302)\n  } catch (err) {\n    console.error(\"[bundle] storage error:\", err)\n    apiError(event, \"Storage is not configured.\", 503, \"storage_unavailable\")\n  }\n})\n"
}

  "content": "import { and, eq } from \"drizzle-orm\"\nimport { collectionItems, collections } from \"~~/shared/db/schema/collection\"\n\nexport async function getOrCreateSystemCollection(\n  userId: string,\n  kind: \"installed\" | \"saved\",\n): Promise<string> {\n  const db = useDb()\n  const existing = await db\n    .select({ id: collections.id })\n    .from(collections)\n    .where(\n      and(eq(collections.ownerUserId, userId), eq(collections.systemKind, kind)),\n    )\n    .limit(1)\n  if (existing[0]) return existing[0].id\n\n  const id = crypto.randomUUID()\n  await db.insert(collections).values({\n    id,\n    ownerUserId: userId,\n    name: kind === \"installed\" ? \"Installed\" : \"Saved\",\n    systemKind: kind,\n  })\n  return id\n}\n\nexport async function upsertCollectionItem(collectionId: string, extensionId: string) {\n  const db = useDb()\n  await db\n    .insert(collectionItems)\n    .values({ collectionId, extensionId })\n    .onConflictDoNothing()\n}\n\nexport async function getUserCollections(userId: string) {\n  const db = useDb()\n  return db\n    .select({\n      id: collections.id,\n      name: collections.name,\n      systemKind: collections.systemKind,\n    })\n    .from(collections)\n    .where(eq(collections.ownerUserId, userId))\n    .orderBy(collections.createdAt)\n}\n"
}

{
  "file_path": "/Users/hutusi/workspace/ai/naive/agentcenter-nuxt/server/utils/installs.ts",
  "content": "import { and, desc, eq, sql } from \"drizzle-orm\"\nimport { installs } from \"~~/shared/db/schema/activity\"\nimport { collectionItems } from \"~~/shared/db/schema/collection\"\nimport { extensions, extensionVersions } from \"~~/shared/db/schema/extension\"\n\nexport type ExtensionRef = { id: string } | { slug: string }\nexport type InstallSource = \"web\" | \"cli\"\nexport type InstallErrorCode = \"extension_not_found\" | \"no_published_version\"\n\nexport class InstallError extends Error {\n  readonly code: InstallErrorCode\n  constructor(code: InstallErrorCode) {\n    super(code)\n    this.code = code\n    this.name = \"InstallError\"\n  }\n}\n\nexport interface RecordInstallParams {\n  userId: string\n  extension: ExtensionRef\n  source: InstallSource\n  version?: string\n}\n\nexport interface InstallRecord {\n  installId: string\n  isFirstInstall: boolean\n  version: string\n}\n\nexport async function recordInstall(params: RecordInstallParams): Promise<InstallRecord> {\n  const { userId, extension, source } = params\n  const db = useDb()\n\n  const extWhere =\n    \"id\" in extension\n      ? eq(extensions.id, extension.id)\n      : eq(extensions.slug, extension.slug)\n\n  const [ext] = await db\n    .select({ id: extensions.id })\n    .from(extensions)\n    .where(extWhere)\n    .limit(1)\n  if (!ext) throw new InstallError(\"extension_not_found\")\n  const extensionId = ext.id\n\n  let version = params.version\n  if (!version) {\n    const [latest] = await db\n      .select({ version: extensionVersions.version })\n      .from(extensionVersions)\n      .where(\n        and(\n          eq(extensionVersions.extensionId, extensionId),\n          eq(extensionVersions.status, \"ready\"),\n        ),\n      )\n      .orderBy(\n        desc(extensionVersions.publishedAt),\n        desc(extensionVersions.createdAt),\n      )\n      .limit(1)\n    if (!latest) throw new InstallError(\"no_published_version\")\n    version = latest.version\n  }\n\n  const installedColId = await getOrCreateSystemCollection(userId, \"installed\")\n  const installId = crypto.randomUUID()\n  const resolvedVersion = version\n\n  const isFirstInstall = await db.transaction(async (tx) => {\n    const prior = await tx\n      .select({ id: installs.id })\n      .from(installs)\n      .where(and(eq(installs.userId, userId), eq(installs.extensionId, extensionId)))\n      .limit(1)\n    const isFirst = prior.length === 0\n\n    await tx.insert(installs).values({\n      id: installId,\n      userId,\n      extensionId,\n      version: resolvedVersion,\n      source,\n    })\n\n    await tx\n      .insert(collectionItems)\n      .values({ collectionId: installedColId, extensionId })\n      .onConflictDoNothing()\n\n    await tx\n      .update(extensions)\n      .set({ downloadsCount: sql`${extensions.downloadsCount} + 1` })\n      .where(eq(extensions.id, extensionId))\n\n    return isFirst\n  })\n\n  return { installId, isFirstInstall, version: resolvedVersion }\n}\n"
}

`25-28`: _💤 Low value_

**Potential race condition in lazy singleton initialization.**

If multiple requests call `useStorage()` concurrently before `_backend` is initialized, `makeBackend()` could be invoked multiple times, creating redundant backend instances. Although harmless in practice (the last one wins), this violates the singleton pattern.




<details>
<summary>🔒 Proposed fix using promise-based singleton</summary>

```diff
 let _backend: StorageBackend | undefined
+let _initPromise: Promise<StorageBackend> | undefined

 export async function useStorage(): Promise<StorageBackend> {
-  if (!_backend) _backend = await makeBackend()
+  if (_backend) return _backend
+  if (!_initPromise) {
+    _initPromise = makeBackend().then(backend => {
+      _backend = backend
+      return backend
+    })
+  }
-  return _backend
+  return _initPromise
 }
```
</details>

add a concise comment immediately above that line explaining that Supabase's
client.storage.createSignedUploadUrl does not accept a custom expiry and always
uses its own fixed TTL, so the expiresInSeconds parameter is intentionally
ignored for compatibility with other storage backends. Mention the function name
getSignedUploadUrl and the Supabase call createSignedUploadUrl so reviewers can
locate the rationale, and keep the "void expiresInSeconds" line to avoid
unused-parameter lint issues.

> AGENT

CodeRabbit was wrong about the `cliAuth` namespace — both en/zh have it at root (line 182 in both). My triage:

## Will fix (one commit)

1. **`bundle.get.ts`** — real correctness bug: ordering is `createdAt` ASC, returns the OLDEST version. Should be `publishedAt DESC NULLS LAST` + filter `status="ready"`.
2. **`code.post.ts`** — wrap the two inserts in `db.transaction` (atomicity).
3. **`device-authorize.post.ts`** — wrap the three writes in `db.transaction` (atomicity).
4. **`cli/auth.vue`** — distinguish `invalid_code` vs `expired`; add `cliAuth.errorExpired` key.
5. **`poll.post.ts`** — Zod-validate the JSON.parse'd state (defensive).
6. **`/api/v1/extensions*` `starsAvg`** — null-safe; column is NOT NULL with default but defensive.
7. **`storage.ts`** — fix the inline comment so it matches the actual "R2 wins when both env sets are present" behavior.

## Skip with reasons

- `apiError` "missing return" — already typed `never`; TS narrows correctly.
- User-code `crypto.getRandomValues` — 32^8 ≈ 10^12 keyspace with 10-min TTL; `Math.random` is sufficient.
- Lazy `useStorage` singleton race — idempotent; harmless.
- `getOrCreateSystemCollection` TOCTOU — at most one extra empty row per user; same as original.
- Move `getOrCreateSystemCollection` inside transaction — marginal gain.
- `bundle.get.ts` differentiated storage errors / explicit `[row]` undefined — `storage_unavailable` is the documented code; `row?.r2Key` is idiomatic.
- `installs.post.ts` `extensionId.uuid()` — IDs are nanoid.
- `InstallButton.vue` truncation + `initialInstalled` prop — P13 polish.
- `cliAuth` namespace mismatch — **false positive**, both files have it at root.

> AGENT

Pushed. Summary of the review fix:

**Real bug fixed:** `bundle.get.ts` was ordering `createdAt` ASC — returning the **oldest** version, not the latest. Fixed to `publishedAt DESC NULLS LAST` + `status="ready"` filter, matching the documented "latest published" contract.

**Atomicity (transactions added):**
- `code.post.ts`: 2 verifications inserts now atomic
- `device-authorize.post.ts`: 3 writes (session/update/delete) now atomic

**Defensive:**
- `poll.post.ts`: Zod-validate the JSON.parse'd state; cleanup delete wrapped in try/catch
- `extensions/*.get.ts`: null-safe `starsAvg`

**UX:**
- `cli/auth.vue` + i18n: distinguish `invalid_code` vs `expired` with new `cliAuth.errorExpired` key

**Doc:**
- `storage.ts` comment now matches actual R2-wins-when-both-set behavior

**Skipped** (in commit body with reasons): `apiError` "missing return" (typed `never`), `Math.random` for user codes (sufficient for 10-min ephemeral codes), `useStorage` singleton race (idempotent), TOCTOU on `getOrCreateSystemCollection` (minor), differentiated storage errors (docs say `storage_unavailable`), nanoid vs UUID, InstallButton truncation/initialInstalled (P13), "cliAuth namespace mismatch" false positive, docstring coverage warning.

87 tests still passing. CI re-running on the fix push.

6	export type ScanResult =
7	  | { ok: true; checksum: string; scanReport: unknown }
8	  | { ok: false; reason: string; scanReport: unknown };
9	
10	// Thrown when a transition is requested against a row that is missing or
11	// not in the expected source state. The state machine is:
12	//
13	//   pending --submit-->   scanning --recordScanResult--> ready | rejected
14	//   ready   --publishVersion--> ready (publishedAt stamped)
15	//
16	// Callers should treat this as "transition refused"; idempotent retries
17	// (e.g. duplicate Inngest deliveries) should catch and no-op.
18	export class VersionStateError extends Error {
19	  readonly code: "version_not_found";
20	  constructor(code: "version_not_found") {
21	    super(code);
22	    this.code = code;
23	    this.name = "VersionStateError";
24	  }
25	}
26	
27	// Move a version to scanning. Allowed source states are `pending` (the
28	// normal first submit) and `scanning` itself (an idempotent retry, e.g.
29	// when a previous attempt's Inngest send failed and left the row stuck —
30	// without this the user would have no way to recover). Versions already
31	// in `ready` or `rejected` reject the transition. Caller is responsible
32	// for kicking off the scan job (Inngest event) — this module owns DB state.
33	export async function submit(versionId: string): Promise<void> {
34	  const updated = await db
35	    .update(extensionVersions)
36	    .set({ status: "scanning" })
37	    .where(
38	      and(
39	        eq(extensionVersions.id, versionId),
40	        inArray(extensionVersions.status, ["pending", "scanning"]),
41	      ),
42	    )
43	    .returning({ id: extensionVersions.id });
44	  if (updated.length === 0) throw new VersionStateError("version_not_found");
45	}
46	
47	// Apply the outcome of a bundle scan: file scan flag + version status.
48	// Both writes commit together; the version must currently be `scanning`.
49	//
50	// Auto-publish on success: extensions with `scope = "personal"` skip the
51	// admin-review step entirely — they go straight to `published` once their
52	// bundle scan is clean. Org/Enterprise drafts stay in `ready` for an
53	// admin to flip them via `publishVersion`.
54	export async function recordScanResult(
55	  versionId: string,
56	  fileId: string,
57	  result: ScanResult,
58	): Promise<void> {
59	  const [version] = await db
60	    .select({
61	      status: extensionVersions.status,
62	      extensionId: extensionVersions.extensionId,
63	      scope: extensions.scope,
64	    })
65	    .from(extensionVersions)
66	    .innerJoin(extensions, eq(extensions.id, extensionVersions.extensionId))
67	    .where(eq(extensionVersions.id, versionId))
68	    .limit(1);
69	  if (!version || version.status !== "scanning") {
70	    throw new VersionStateError("version_not_found");
71	  }
72	
73	  await db.transaction(async (tx) => {
74	    if (result.ok) {
75	      const isPersonal = version.scope === "personal";
76	      const now = isPersonal ? new Date() : null;
77	
78	      await tx
79	        .update(files)
80	        .set({
81	          scanStatus: "clean",
82	          scanReport: result.scanReport,
83	          checksumSha256: result.checksum,
84	        })
85	        .where(eq(files.id, fileId));
86	      await tx
87	        .update(extensionVersions)
88	        .set(
89	          isPersonal
90	            ? { status: "ready", publishedAt: now }
91	            : { status: "ready" },
92	        )
93	        .where(eq(extensionVersions.id, versionId));
94	      if (isPersonal) {
95	        await tx
96	          .update(extensions)
97	          .set({ visibility: "published", publishedAt: now })
98	          .where(eq(extensions.id, version.extensionId));
99	      }
100	    } else {
101	      await tx
102	        .update(files)
103	        .set({ scanStatus: "flagged", scanReport: result.scanReport })
104	        .where(eq(files.id, fileId));
105	      await tx
106	        .update(extensionVersions)
107	        .set({ status: "rejected" })
108	        .where(eq(extensionVersions.id, versionId));
109	    }
110	  });
111	}
112	
113	// Flip the version + its parent extension to published. Returns the
114	// extension id so the caller can revalidate caches and dispatch
115	// downstream events (those are orchestration, not state). The version
116	// must currently be `ready`.
117	//
118	// Note: extensions.search_vector is a GENERATED column maintained by
119	// Postgres; this module never writes to it.
120	export async function publishVersion(
121	  versionId: string,
122	): Promise<{ extensionId: string }> {
123	  const [row] = await db
124	    .select({
125	      extensionId: extensionVersions.extensionId,
126	      status: extensionVersions.status,
127	    })
128	    .from(extensionVersions)
129	    .where(eq(extensionVersions.id, versionId))
130	    .limit(1);
131	
132	  if (!row || row.status !== "ready") {
133	    throw new VersionStateError("version_not_found");
134	  }
135	
136	  const { extensionId } = row;
137	  const now = new Date();
138	
139	  await db.transaction(async (tx) => {
140	    await tx
141	      .update(extensions)
142	      .set({ visibility: "published", publishedAt: now })
143	      .where(eq(extensions.id, extensionId));
144	    await tx
145	      .update(extensionVersions)
146	      .set({ publishedAt: now })
147	      .where(eq(extensionVersions.id, versionId));
148	  });
149	
150	  return { extensionId };
151	}
152

1	import { eq } from "drizzle-orm";
2	import { unzipSync } from "fflate";
3	import { parse } from "smol-toml";
4	
5	import { inngest } from "./client";
6	import { db } from "@/lib/db/client";
7	import { files } from "@/lib/db/schema";
8	import { recordScanResult, VersionStateError } from "@/lib/extensions/state";
9	import { generatePresignedGetUrl } from "@/lib/storage/r2";
10	import { BundleManifestSchema } from "@/lib/validators/manifest";
11	
12	export const scanBundle = inngest.createFunction(
13	  {
14	    id: "scan-bundle",
15	    triggers: [{ event: "extension/scan.requested" }],
16	  },
17	  async ({ event, step }) => {
18	    const { versionId, fileId } = event.data as { versionId: string; fileId: string };
19	
20	    // Steps 1–4: fetch, download, checksum, and manifest parsing in one step
21	    // to avoid Buffer serialization issues across step boundaries.
22	    const scanResult = await step.run("download-and-scan", async () => {
23	      const [fileRow] = await db.select().from(files).where(eq(files.id, fileId)).limit(1);
24	      if (!fileRow) return { ok: false as const, reason: "file_not_found", checksum: "" };
25	
26	      const signedUrl = await generatePresignedGetUrl(fileRow.r2Key, 120);
27	      const res = await fetch(signedUrl);
28	      if (!res.ok) throw new Error(`R2 fetch failed: ${res.status}`);
29	      const arrayBuf = await res.arrayBuffer();
30	      const uint8 = new Uint8Array(arrayBuf);
31	
32	      // SHA-256 checksum
33	      const hashBuf = await crypto.subtle.digest("SHA-256", uint8);
34	      const checksum = Array.from(new Uint8Array(hashBuf))
35	        .map((b) => b.toString(16).padStart(2, "0"))
36	        .join("");
37	
38	      // Parse manifest.toml
39	      const entries = unzipSync(uint8);
40	      const manifestEntry = entries["manifest.toml"];
41	      if (!manifestEntry) return { ok: false as const, reason: "missing_manifest", checksum };
42	
43	      let raw: unknown;
44	      try {
45	        raw = parse(new TextDecoder().decode(manifestEntry));
46	      } catch {
47	        return { ok: false as const, reason: "invalid_toml", checksum };
48	      }
49	
50	      const parsed = BundleManifestSchema.safeParse(raw);
51	      if (!parsed.success) {
52	        return { ok: false as const, reason: parsed.error.issues[0]?.message ?? "schema_error", checksum };
53	      }
54	
55	      return { ok: true as const, checksum };
56	    });
57	
58	    const scanReport = {
59	      manifestOk: scanResult.ok,
60	      reason: scanResult.ok ? null : scanResult.reason,
61	      checksum: scanResult.checksum,
62	      scannedAt: new Date().toISOString(),
63	    };
64	
65	    // VersionStateError here means the version is no longer in `scanning` —
66	    // typically a duplicate Inngest delivery for an already-scanned version.
67	    // Treat as no-op so retries don't fail the function.
68	    await step.run("record-scan-result", async () => {
69	      try {
70	        if (scanResult.ok) {
71	          await recordScanResult(versionId, fileId, {
72	            ok: true,
73	            checksum: scanResult.checksum,
74	            scanReport,
75	          });
76	        } else {
77	          await recordScanResult(versionId, fileId, {
78	            ok: false,
79	            reason: scanResult.reason,
80	            scanReport,
81	          });
82	        }
83	      } catch (err) {
84	        if (err instanceof VersionStateError) return;
85	        throw err;
86	      }
87	    });
88	
89	    if (!scanResult.ok) {
90	      return { ok: false, reason: scanResult.reason };
91	    }
92	
93	    await step.sendEvent("enqueue-index", {
94	      name: "extension/index.requested",
95	      data: { versionId },
96	    });
97	
98	    return { ok: true, checksum: scanResult.checksum };
99	  },
100	);
101

31	// Coerce empty / missing optional strings to `null`. We can't use `?? null`
32	// (it keeps `""`, which then FK-violates against `departments.id`) and we
33	// avoid `|| null` because it would also drop a legitimate `"0"`.
34	function emptyToNull(v: string | undefined | null): string | null {
35	  return v == null || v === "" ? null : v;

39	// stable default keyed off the extension category so existing filter
40	// queries (which key on funcCat/subCat) keep matching newly-published
41	// rows. Admins can refine these later via curation tooling.
42	function defaultClassification(category: ManifestFormValues["category"]): {
43	  funcCat: "tools" | "workTask" | "business";
44	  subCat: string;
45	} {
46	  switch (category) {
47	    case "mcp":
48	      return { funcCat: "tools", subCat: "integrations" };
49	    case "slash":
50	      return { funcCat: "tools", subCat: "commands" };
51	    case "skills":
52	    case "plugins":
53	    default:
54	      return { funcCat: "tools", subCat: "general" };
55	  }

62	export async function createDraftExtension(
63	  raw: ManifestFormValues,
64	): Promise<CreateDraftResult> {
65	  const session = await auth.api.getSession({ headers: await headers() });
66	  if (!session) return { ok: false, error: "unauthenticated" };
67	
68	  const parsed = ManifestFormSchema.safeParse(raw);
69	  if (!parsed.success) {
70	    // Return a stable error code (so the UI can localize it) and put the
71	    // human-readable Zod messages in `detail` so the user can see *what*
72	    // failed even outside development.
73	    return {
74	      ok: false,
75	      error: "invalid_input",
76	      detail: parsed.error.issues.map((i) => i.message).join("; "),
77	    };
78	  }
79	  const data = parsed.data;
80	  const cls = defaultClassification(data.category);
81	
82	  const extensionId = crypto.randomUUID();
83	  const versionId = crypto.randomUUID();
84	
85	  try {
86	    await db.transaction(async (tx) => {
87	      await tx.insert(extensions).values({
88	        id: extensionId,
89	        slug: data.slug,
90	        name: data.name,
91	        nameZh: emptyToNull(data.nameZh),
92	        // The wizard's "summary" maps onto the existing tagline column.
93	        tagline: data.summary,
94	        taglineZh: emptyToNull(data.taglineZh),
95	        category: data.category,
96	        scope: data.scope,
97	        // The wizard does not collect funcCat/subCat — server defaults
98	        // backfill them off the chosen category so filter queries still match.
99	        funcCat: cls.funcCat,
100	        subCat: cls.subCat,
101	        // Empty strings are FK violations against departments.id — coerce to null.
102	        deptId: emptyToNull(data.deptId),
103	        iconColor: data.iconColor,
104	        readmeMd: emptyToNull(data.readmeMd ?? ""),
105	        permissions: data.permissions ?? {},
106	        publisherUserId: session.user.id,
107	        ownerOrgId: DEFAULT_ORG_ID,
108	        visibility: "draft",
109	      });
110	
111	      await tx.insert(extensionVersions).values({
112	        id: versionId,
113	        extensionId,
114	        version: data.version,
115	        status: "pending",
116	        sourceMethod: data.sourceMethod,
117	      });
118	
119	      if (data.tagIds.length > 0) {
120	        await tx.insert(extensionTags).values(
121	          data.tagIds.map((tagId) => ({ extensionId, tagId })),
122	        );
123	      }
124	    });
125	  } catch (err) {
126	    const code = classifyDraftError(err);
127	    console.error("[publish] createDraftExtension failed", {
128	      code,
129	      pgCode: pgErrorCode(err),
130	      constraint: pgConstraint(err),
131	      slug: data.slug,
132	      message: err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err),
133	    });
134	    return { ok: false, error: code, detail: devErrorDetail(err) };
135	  }
136	
137	  return { ok: true, extensionId, versionId };
138	}

188	export async function submitForReview(versionId: string): Promise<SubmitResult> {
189	  const session = await auth.api.getSession({ headers: await headers() });
190	  if (!session) return { ok: false, error: "unauthenticated" };
191	
192	  // Load bundleFileId needed by the scan job
193	  const [version] = await db
194	    .select({ bundleFileId: extensionVersions.bundleFileId })
195	    .from(extensionVersions)
196	    .where(eq(extensionVersions.id, versionId))
197	    .limit(1);
198	
199	  if (!version?.bundleFileId) return { ok: false, error: "no_bundle" };
200	
201	  try {
202	    await submit(versionId);
203	  } catch (err) {
204	    console.error("[publish] submitForReview failed", {
205	      pgCode: pgErrorCode(err),
206	      versionId,
207	      message: err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err),
208	    });
209	    // The state machine refused the transition — the version isn't in a
210	    // submittable state (already reviewed/rejected, or the row vanished).
211	    // This is not a generic DB error and shouldn't be reported as one.
212	    if (err instanceof VersionStateError) {
213	      return {
214	        ok: false,
215	        error: "version_not_submittable",
216	        detail: devErrorDetail(err),
217	      };
218	    }
219	    return { ok: false, error: "db_error", detail: devErrorDetail(err) };
220	  }
221	
222	  // Queue the scan job. If this fails (e.g. INNGEST_EVENT_KEY missing,
223	  // Inngest unreachable), roll the version status back to `pending` so it
224	  // doesn't sit stuck in `scanning` with no scan ever happening.
225	  try {
226	    const { inngest } = await import("@/lib/jobs/client");
227	    await inngest.send({
228	      name: "extension/scan.requested",
229	      data: { versionId, fileId: version.bundleFileId },
230	    });
231	  } catch (err) {
232	    console.error("[publish] inngest.send failed", err);
233	    try {
234	      await db
235	        .update(extensionVersions)
236	        .set({ status: "pending" })
237	        .where(
238	          and(
239	            eq(extensionVersions.id, versionId),
240	            eq(extensionVersions.status, "scanning"),
241	          ),
242	        );
243	    } catch (rollbackErr) {
244	      console.error(
245	        "[publish] failed to roll back scanning -> pending after inngest error",
246	        rollbackErr,
247	      );
248	    }
249	    return {
250	      ok: false,
251	      error: "scan_queue_unavailable",
252	      detail: devErrorDetail(err),
253	    };
254	  }
255	
256	  return { ok: true };
257	}

259	export async function getMyExtensions(userId: string) {
260	  // Pull the latest version per extension alongside the extension row so the
261	  // dashboard can show "where am I in the wizard" (e.g. needs upload vs.
262	  // submitted, awaiting scan) — visibility alone hides that info. Also
263	  // joins the bundle file via `bundleFileId` (logical reference, no FK)
264	  // so the dashboard can surface the scan rejection reason inline for
265	  // rejected versions without an extra round-trip.
266	  const rows = await db
267	    .select({
268	      id: extensions.id,
269	      slug: extensions.slug,
270	      name: extensions.name,
271	      category: extensions.category,
272	      visibility: extensions.visibility,
273	      createdAt: extensions.createdAt,
274	      latestVersionId: extensionVersions.id,
275	      latestVersion: extensionVersions.version,
276	      latestStatus: extensionVersions.status,
277	      latestBundleFileId: extensionVersions.bundleFileId,
278	      latestScanReport: files.scanReport,
279	    })
280	    .from(extensions)
281	    .leftJoin(
282	      extensionVersions,
283	      eq(extensionVersions.extensionId, extensions.id),
284	    )
285	    .leftJoin(files, eq(files.id, extensionVersions.bundleFileId))
286	    .where(eq(extensions.publisherUserId, userId))
287	    .orderBy(desc(extensions.createdAt), desc(extensionVersions.createdAt));
288	
289	  // Collapse to one row per extension (latest version first thanks to the
290	  // ORDER BY). If we someday support multiple in-flight versions per
291	  // extension, this becomes a `DISTINCT ON` query.
292	  const byExtension = new Map<
293	    string,
294	    (typeof rows)[number] & { latestScanReason: string | null }
295	  >();
296	  for (const row of rows) {
297	    if (!byExtension.has(row.id)) {
298	      byExtension.set(row.id, {
299	        ...row,
300	        latestScanReason: extractScanReason(row.latestScanReport),
301	      });
302	    }
303	  }
304	  return Array.from(byExtension.values());
305	}

307	export type UpdateDraftResult =
308	  | { ok: true }
309	  | { ok: false; error: string; detail?: string };
310	
311	// Update an in-flight draft's manifest fields. Owner-checked. Refuses to
312	// touch anything once the version has left `pending` — by then the
313	// scanner has likely picked it up and re-running scans is the worker's
314	// job, not the wizard's. `slug` and `version` can technically be
315	// changed, but the wizard locks them in resume mode because they form
316	// the R2 bundle key — letting them shift orphans the uploaded bundle.
317	export async function updateDraftExtension(
318	  extensionId: string,
319	  raw: ManifestFormValues,
320	): Promise<UpdateDraftResult> {
321	  const session = await auth.api.getSession({ headers: await headers() });
322	  if (!session) return { ok: false, error: "unauthenticated" };
323	
324	  const parsed = ManifestFormSchema.safeParse(raw);
325	  if (!parsed.success) {
326	    return {
327	      ok: false,
328	      error: "invalid_input",
329	      detail: parsed.error.issues.map((i) => i.message).join("; "),
330	    };
331	  }
332	  const data = parsed.data;
333	
334	  // Resolve the latest version + verify ownership + state in one read.
335	  const [row] = await db
336	    .select({
337	      publisherUserId: extensions.publisherUserId,
338	      versionId: extensionVersions.id,
339	      versionStatus: extensionVersions.status,
340	    })
341	    .from(extensions)
342	    .leftJoin(
343	      extensionVersions,
344	      eq(extensionVersions.extensionId, extensions.id),
345	    )
346	    .where(eq(extensions.id, extensionId))
347	    .orderBy(desc(extensionVersions.createdAt))
348	    .limit(1);
349	
350	  if (!row || !row.versionId) {
351	    return { ok: false, error: "not_found" };
352	  }
353	  if (row.publisherUserId !== session.user.id) {
354	    return { ok: false, error: "not_found" };
355	  }
356	  if (row.versionStatus !== "pending") {
357	    return { ok: false, error: "version_not_editable" };
358	  }
359	  // Lift the narrowed value to a local — TS loses the `!== null` proof
360	  // across the transaction closure boundary, and a non-null assertion
361	  // inside the closure is harder to audit than a guarded constant.
362	  const versionId = row.versionId;
363	
364	  try {
365	    await db.transaction(async (tx) => {
366	      // SECURITY: `slug` and `version` are deliberately NOT written from
367	      // `data`. The wizard renders those inputs as `readOnly` in resume
368	      // mode, but `readOnly` is a client-side hint only — a caller
369	      // hitting this action directly (devtools, scripted POST) could
370	      // otherwise change the slug or version, which would orphan the
371	      // already-uploaded R2 bundle at its old `<slug>/<version>` key.
372	      await tx
373	        .update(extensions)
374	        .set({
375	          name: data.name,
376	          nameZh: emptyToNull(data.nameZh),
377	          tagline: data.summary,
378	          taglineZh: emptyToNull(data.taglineZh),
379	          category: data.category,
380	          scope: data.scope,
381	          // funcCat/subCat are intentionally NOT touched on update — admin
382	          // curation may have set non-default values, and the wizard never
383	          // surfaces them so a re-write would silently revert that work.
384	          deptId: emptyToNull(data.deptId),
385	          iconColor: data.iconColor,
386	          readmeMd: emptyToNull(data.readmeMd ?? ""),
387	          permissions: data.permissions ?? {},
388	          updatedAt: new Date(),
389	        })
390	        .where(eq(extensions.id, extensionId));
391	
392	      // Persist source method on the version too (the wizard re-sends it).
393	      await tx
394	        .update(extensionVersions)
395	        .set({ sourceMethod: data.sourceMethod })
396	        .where(eq(extensionVersions.id, versionId));
397	
398	      // Tags: replace wholesale. The set is capped at 8 by the form
399	      // schema, so a delete-then-insert is cheaper and clearer than
400	      // computing a diff.
401	      await tx
402	        .delete(extensionTags)
403	        .where(eq(extensionTags.extensionId, extensionId));
404	      if (data.tagIds.length > 0) {
405	        await tx
406	          .insert(extensionTags)
407	          .values(data.tagIds.map((tagId) => ({ extensionId, tagId })));
408	      }
409	    });
410	  } catch (err) {
411	    const code = classifyDraftError(err);
412	    console.error("[publish] updateDraftExtension failed", {
413	      code,
414	      pgCode: pgErrorCode(err),
415	      constraint: pgConstraint(err),
416	      extensionId,
417	      message: err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err),
418	    });
419	    return { ok: false, error: code, detail: devErrorDetail(err) };
420	  }
421	
422	  return { ok: true };
423	}

429	// Permanently delete a draft extension. Owner-checked. Only allowed while
430	// visibility === "draft" — published or archived extensions are not
431	// throwaway. Cascading FK constraints clean up extension_versions,
432	// extension_tags, and (via versions) any associated files row.
433	//
434	// R2 bundle objects are intentionally left in place; orphan cleanup is
435	// the bucket lifecycle's job, not the user's.
436	export async function discardDraft(
437	  extensionId: string,
438	): Promise<DiscardDraftResult> {
439	  const session = await auth.api.getSession({ headers: await headers() });
440	  if (!session) return { ok: false, error: "unauthenticated" };
441	
442	  const [row] = await db
443	    .select({
444	      publisherUserId: extensions.publisherUserId,
445	      visibility: extensions.visibility,
446	    })
447	    .from(extensions)
448	    .where(eq(extensions.id, extensionId))
449	    .limit(1);
450	
451	  // Treat not-found and not-owner identically so the contract can't be
452	  // used to probe whether an extension exists for someone else.
453	  if (!row || row.publisherUserId !== session.user.id) {
454	    return { ok: false, error: "not_found" };
455	  }
456	  if (row.visibility !== "draft") {
457	    return { ok: false, error: "not_discardable" };
458	  }
459	
460	  await db.delete(extensions).where(eq(extensions.id, extensionId));
461	  return { ok: true };
462	}

\"integrations\" }\n    case \"slash\":\n      return { funcCat: \"tools\", subCat: \"commands\" }\n    default:\n      return { funcCat: \"tools\", subCat: \"general\" }\n  }\n}\n\nexport type CreateDraftResult =\n  | { ok: true; extensionId: string; versionId: string }\n  | { ok: false; error: string; detail?: string }\n\nexport async function createDraftExtension(\n  userId: string,\n  raw: ManifestFormValues,\n): Promise<CreateDraftResult> {\n  const parsed = ManifestFormSchema.safeParse(raw)\n  if (!parsed.success) {\n    return {\n      ok: false,\n      error: \"invalid_input\",\n      detail: parsed.error.issues.map((i) => i.message).join(\"; \"),\n    }\n  }\n  const data = parsed.data\n  const cls = defaultClassification(data.category)\n  const extensionId = crypto.randomUUID()\n  const versionId = crypto.randomUUID()\n  const db = useDb()\n\n  try {\n    await db.transaction(async (tx) => {\n      await tx.insert(extensions).values({\n        id: extensionId,\n        slug: data.slug,\n        name: data.name,\n        nameZh: emptyToNull(data.nameZh),\n        tagline: data.summary,\n        taglineZh: emptyToNull(data.taglineZh),\n        category: data.category,\n        scope: data.scope,\n        funcCat: cls.funcCat,\n        subCat: cls.subCat,\n        deptId: emptyToNull(data.deptId),\n        iconColor: data.iconColor,\n        readmeMd: emptyToNull(data.readmeMd ?? \"\"),\n        permissions: data.permissions ?? {},\n        publisherUserId: userId,\n        ownerOrgId: DEFAULT_ORG_ID,\n        visibility: \"draft\",\n      })\n      await tx.insert(extensionVersions).values({\n        id: versionId,\n        extensionId,\n        version: data.version,\n        status: \"pending\",\n        sourceMethod: data.sourceMethod,\n      })\n      if (data.tagIds.length > 0) {\n        await tx.insert(extensionTags).values(\n          data.tagIds.map((tagId) => ({ extensionId, tagId })),\n        )\n      }\n    })\n  } catch (err) {\n    console.error(\"[publish] createDraftExtension failed\", err)\n    const message = err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err)\n    if (message.includes(\"extensions_slug_unique\") || message.includes(\"duplicate key\")) {\n      return { ok: false, error: \"slug_taken\" }\n    }\n    return { ok: false, error: \"db_error\", detail: message }\n  }\n  return { ok: true, extensionId, versionId }\n}\n\nexport type AttachFileResult =\n  | { ok: true; fileId: string }\n  | { ok: false; error: string }\n\nexport async function attachFile(\n  versionId: string,\n  r2Key: string,\n  size: number,\n  checksumSha256: string,\n): Promise<AttachFileResult> {\n  const fileId = crypto.randomUUID()\n  const db = useDb()\n  try {\n    await db.transaction(async (tx) => {\n      await tx.insert(files).values({\n        id: fileId,\n        r2Key,\n        size: BigInt(size),\n        checksumSha256,\n        mimeType: \"application/zip\",\n        scanStatus: \"pending\",\n      })\n      await tx\n        .update(extensionVersions)\n        .set({ bundleFileId: fileId })\n        .where(eq(extensionVersions.id, versionId))\n    })\n  } catch (err) {\n    console.error(\"[publish] attachFile failed\", err)\n    return { ok: false, error: \"db_error\" }\n  }\n  return { ok: true, fileId }\n}\n\nexport type SubmitResult =\n  | { ok: true }\n  | { ok: false; error: string }\n\nexport async function submitForReview(versionId: string): Promise<SubmitResult> {\n  const db = useDb()\n  const [version] = await db\n    .select({ bundleFileId: extensionVersions.bundleFileId })\n    .from(extensionVersions)\n    .where(eq(extensionVersions.id, versionId))\n    .limit(1)\n  if (!version?.bundleFileId) return { ok: false, error: \"no_bundle\" }\n\n  try {\n    await submit(versionId)\n  } catch (err) {\n    if (err instanceof VersionStateError) {\n      return { ok: false, error: \"version_not_submittable\" }\n    }\n    console.error(\"[publish] submitForReview failed\", err)\n    return { ok: false, error: \"db_error\" }\n  }\n\n  try {\n    const { inngest } = await import(\"~~/server/utils/inngest\")\n    await inngest.send({\n      name: \"extension/scan.requested\",\n      data: { versionId, fileId: version.bundleFileId },\n    })\n  } catch (err) {\n    console.error(\"[publish] inngest.send failed\", err)\n    try {\n      await db\n        .update(extensionVersions)\n        .set({ status: \"pending\" })\n        .where(\n          and(\n            eq(extensionVersions.id, versionId),\n            eq(extensionVersions.status, \"scanning\"),\n          ),\n        )\n    } catch (rollbackErr) {\n      console.error(\"[publish] rollback after inngest failure failed\", rollbackErr)\n    }\n    return { ok: false, error: \"scan_queue_unavailable\" }\n  }\n  return { ok: true }\n}\n\nexport async function getMyExtensions(userId: string) {\n  const db = useDb()\n  const rows = await db\n    .select({\n      id: extensions.id,\n      slug: extensions.slug,\n      name: extensions.name,\n      category: extensions.category,\n      visibility: extensions.visibility,\n      createdAt: extensions.createdAt,\n      latestVersionId: extensionVersions.id,\n      latestVersion: extensionVersions.version,\n      latestStatus: extensionVersions.status,\n      latestBundleFileId: extensionVersions.bundleFileId,\n    })\n    .from(extensions)\n    .leftJoin(\n      extensionVersions,\n      eq(extensionVersions.extensionId, extensions.id),\n    )\n    .where(eq(extensions.publisherUserId, userId))\n    .orderBy(desc(extensions.createdAt), desc(extensionVersions.createdAt))\n\n  const byExtension = new Map<string, (typeof rows)[number]>()\n  for (const row of rows) {\n    if (!byExtension.has(row.id)) byExtension.set(row.id, row)\n  }\n  return Array.from(byExtension.values())\n}\n\nexport async function discardDraft(\n  userId: string,\n  extensionId: string,\n): Promise<{ ok: true } | { ok: false; error: string }> {\n  const db = useDb()\n  const [row] = await db\n    .select({\n      publisherUserId: extensions.publisherUserId,\n      visibility: extensions.visibility,\n    })\n    .from(extensions)\n    .where(eq(extensions.id, extensionId))\n    .limit(1)\n\n  if (!row || row.publisherUserId !== userId) {\n    return { ok: false, error: \"not_found\" }\n  }\n  if (row.visibility !== \"draft\") {\n    return { ok: false, error: \"not_discardable\" }\n  }\n\n  await db.delete(extensions).where(eq(extensions.id, extensionId))\n  return { ok: true }\n}\n"
}

}

{
  "command": "gh pr create --base main --head feat/p4-publishing --title \"feat: P10-P11 publishing pipeline\" --body \"$(cat <<'EOF'\n## Summary\n\n4 commits, ~900 LOC. Closes the publish loop end-to-end: a signed-in user can fill a form, upload a zip bundle, hit \"submit for review,\" and have Inngest scan + auto-publish (for personal-scope) extensions.\n\n- **P10 — Manifest validators** (`shared/validators/manifest.ts`, 103 LOC verbatim from original + 270 LOC of tests). Three Zod schemas: `ExtensionManifestCore` (the single source of truth), `ManifestFormSchema` (what the wizard collects), `BundleManifestSchema` (what scan-bundle expects inside the zip).\n- **P11 — State machine** (`server/utils/extensions-state.ts`, verbatim port of the 151-LOC original). `submit` / `recordScanResult` / `publishVersion` — every transition checks source state and is transactional. Auto-publish branch for `scope=personal`; org/enterprise wait for admin `publishVersion`.\n- **P10 + P11 — Publish endpoints + Inngest** (one commit, ~600 LOC). `server/utils/publish.ts` with the 5 minimum-viable actions (`createDraft`, `attachFile`, `submitForReview`, `getMyExtensions`, `discardDraft`). `server/utils/inngest.ts` (lazy-loaded functions list to keep `fflate` / `smol-toml` out of every request's import graph). `scan-bundle` + `reindex-search` jobs ported. Webhook at `server/api/inngest.ts` using `inngest/node`'s `serve()`.\n- **P10 — Publisher dashboard + new-draft form**. `/publish` lists my drafts/extensions with derived stage labels; `/publish/new` is a single-page form that runs the full create → sign → upload → attach → submit chain on submit, with a live stage indicator and one inline error panel.\n\n## Why\n\nThis is the \"publish\" half of the install/publish round-trip. After this PR, the marketplace can take submissions; previously every extension came from the seed script. The `scan-bundle` worker exercises the storage abstraction from PR #5 — proves Supabase Storage + Inngest play together on Nitro. Personal-scope auto-publish means the extension appears on `/extensions` the moment the scan completes, with no admin curation step.\n\n## Test plan\n\n- [x] `bun run validate` exits 0 (114 tests passing — 27 new manifest validator tests)\n- [x] CI green expected\n- [ ] **Reviewer with local Postgres + Inngest dev server + Supabase Storage configured**:\n  - `bunx inngest-cli@latest dev` in another terminal (auto-discovers `/api/inngest`)\n  - Sign in, navigate to `/publish/new`\n  - Fill: name \"Test Skill\", slug \"test-skill\", version \"0.1.0\", category Skills, scope **Personal** (important for auto-publish), summary \"test\"\n  - Pick a zip containing a valid `manifest.toml` (sections `[extension]` + `[categorization]` per `docs/manifest-spec.md`)\n  - Submit → progress stages flash → land on `/publish` with row showing \"Awaiting scan\"\n  - Inngest dev UI shows `extension/scan.requested` → `extension/index.requested` events fire\n  - Row flips to \"Published\"; `/en/extensions` shows the new extension\n  - Discard a different draft → confirms then 200s; row disappears\n\n## Tradeoffs\n\n- **Minimum-viable form, not the 4-step rail wizard.** The original `<UploadWizard>` with Basics → Bundle → Listing → Review steps + live preview is ~700 LOC of Vue and adds tags, dept, README, permissions, icon color, and resume/edit. Single-page form covers the create + submit path; the richer UX lands in P13 polish or a follow-up.\n- **No `updateDraftExtension` / `getDraft` ports.** Drafts in this PR are write-once: create + upload + submit, or discard. Resume/edit comes with the rail wizard.\n- **Skipped detailed pg error classification** (`classifyDraftError`, `pgErrorCode`, `pgConstraint` from the original `publish-errors.ts`). Replaced with a one-line substring check for the common `slug_taken` case; everything else returns generic `db_error`. Restoring the fine-grained error mapping is a deferred refactor.\n- **Inngest `signingKey` is read from env**, not passed explicitly to `serve()` — the `ServeHandlerOptions` type doesn't accept it on the version we're on. Functionally identical.\n- **No `revalidateTag` equivalent in `reindex-search`.** Nuxt's `useFetch` cache invalidates on navigation; tag-based busting isn't part of the data layer. Pages refetch on next visit.\n\n## Known follow-ups (NOT in this PR)\n\n- 4-step rail wizard with resume/edit/live-preview → P13 or P10 follow-up\n- Tags / dept / README / permissions / icon color in the publish flow → same\n- Contract tests for `/api/v1` (deferred from PR #5)\n- Status polling on the publisher dashboard (manual refresh works today)\n- Filter UI pickers (DeptPicker / TagDrawer / Creator+Publisher) — also deferred since PR #2\nEOF\n)\" 2>&1 | tail -3",
  "description": "Open PR for publishing pipeline",
  "timeout": 60000
}

Title: `feat: P10-P11 publishing pipeline`. 4 commits on `feat/p4-publishing` → `main`.

- `shared/validators/manifest.ts` (ported verbatim with 27 new tests)
- `server/utils/extensions-state.ts` (state machine: submit/recordScanResult/publishVersion)
- `server/utils/publish.ts` (5 minimum-viable actions)
- `server/utils/inngest.ts` + `jobs/{scan-bundle,reindex-search}.ts`
- `server/api/inngest.ts` webhook using `inngest/node` serve
- `/api/internal/publish/*` endpoints (create-draft, attach-file, submit, discard, my-extensions)

- `publish.*` i18n namespace

**Scope honesty** (in PR body):
- Single-page form instead of the 4-step rail wizard (~700 LOC saved)
- No resume/edit (no `updateDraftExtension` / `getDraft` ports)
- Simplified pg error classification
- Status polling on dashboard is manual-refresh only

**114 tests passing locally** (was 87). End-to-end publish loop now exists: with Inngest dev server + storage configured, a personal-scope extension can be submitted and auto-publish to `/extensions`.

> AGENT

Real findings this time. Triage:

## Will fix (one commit, 8 fixes — 2 are real security bugs)

1. **`attach-file.post.ts`: authorization bypass.** Any signed-in user can attach a file to any version. Add ownership check via the version→extension→publisherUserId join.
2. **`submit.post.ts`: same authorization bypass.** Any user can submit any version. Same fix pattern.
3. **`api/inngest.ts`: missing `await` on the handler.** `serve()` returns async; without await Nuxt might return before Inngest finishes.
4. **`publish.ts attachFile`: orphan file row on missing version.** The UPDATE inside the transaction has no row-count guard; if `versionId` doesn't match, the files row is inserted but the version isn't updated. Throw to force rollback when the update affects 0 rows.
5. **`scan-bundle.ts`: Zod-validate `event.data`** instead of `as` cast.
6. **`reindex-search.ts`: same.**
7. **`scan-bundle.ts`: try/catch around `unzipSync`** for corrupt-zip resilience.
8. **`scan-bundle.ts` (nitpick): log VersionStateError catches** (quick win — keeps the idempotency contract but adds a `console.warn` for debugging).
9. **`new.vue`: i18n the category/scope option labels** instead of hardcoded English.

## Skip with reasons

- **`ownerOrgId: DEFAULT_ORG_ID` always** — matches locked decision #1 (multi-tenant schema, single-tenant UI for v1). The wizard intentionally doesn't surface an org picker.
- **"Move pages under `[locale]/`"** — recurring false positive (`@nuxtjs/i18n` owns the prefix).
- **Docstring coverage** — CLAUDE.md conflict.

5	  {

7	    triggers: [{ event: "extension/index.requested" }],
8	  },
9	  async ({ event, step }) => {
10	    const { versionId } = event.data as { versionId: string }
11	
12	    let extensionId: string
13	    try {
14	      const result = await step.run("publish-version", () => publishVersion(versionId))
15	      extensionId = result.extensionId
16	    } catch (err) {
17	      if (err instanceof VersionStateError) {
18	        return { ok: false, reason: err.code }

20	      throw err
21	    }

23	    // Nuxt's data layer caches via useFetch keys, not tags. Cache busting on
24	    // the consuming page happens via re-fetch when the user navigates back.
25	    // No revalidateTag equivalent needed here.
26	
27	    await step.sendEvent("notify-published", {
28	      name: "extension/published",
29	      data: { extensionId, versionId },
30	    })
31	
32	    return { ok: true, extensionId }
33	  },
34	)

fix(p4-publishing): address PR #6 review feedback

Real security bugs:
- attach-file.post.ts + publish.ts:attachFile() now requires the
  caller's userId and verifies (version → extension → publisherUserId)
  ownership before writing the files row. Previously any authenticated
  user could attach a bundle to anyone else's version.
- submit.post.ts + publish.ts:submitForReview() now requires userId and
  verifies ownership before kicking off the scan. Same bypass class.

Real correctness:
- publish.ts attachFile transaction: the version-update step now uses
  .returning() and throws if 0 rows were affected. Forces rollback so
  we don't leave an orphan files row when the versionId no longer
  exists (e.g. the draft was discarded between create and attach).
- server/api/inngest.ts: await serve()'s handler. The Inngest serve()
  returns an async function; without await the Nuxt handler could
  return before signature verification + step dispatch finished.

Defensive validation:
- scan-bundle.ts: Zod-validate event.data (versionId + fileId) instead
  of the unsafe `as` cast. Logs and returns invalid_event for bad
  payloads. Wraps unzipSync in try/catch — corrupt zips now record an
  invalid_zip scan failure instead of crashing the function.
- reindex-search.ts: same Zod validation on event.data.
- scan-bundle.ts: log VersionStateError catches (still idempotent;
  log surfaces the case in production triage).

UX polish:
- publish/new.vue + i18n: category and scope <option> labels now use
  t('publish.options.category.*') / t('publish.options.scope.*')
  instead of hardcoded English. en + zh both have the keys.

Skipped findings (with reasons):

- ownerOrgId always DEFAULT_ORG_ID — locked decision #1 (multi-tenant
  schema, single-tenant UI for v1). The form doesn't surface an org
  picker by design.
- "Move pages under [locale]/" — recurring false positive.
- Docstring coverage warning — CLAUDE.md conflict.

> AGENT

Pushed. Summary of the fix:

**Real security bugs:**
- `attachFile`: now takes `userId` and verifies ownership via the version→extension join. Previously any signed-in user could attach a bundle to anyone else's version.
- `submitForReview`: same fix. Same bypass class.

**Real correctness:**
- `attachFile` transaction: uses `.returning()` and throws if 0 rows updated, forcing rollback. No more orphan `files` rows when versionId disappears mid-transaction.
- `api/inngest.ts`: awaits `serve()` handler — without await, Nuxt could return before Inngest finished.

**Defensive:**
- `scan-bundle.ts` + `reindex-search.ts`: Zod-validate `event.data` instead of unsafe `as` cast.
- `scan-bundle.ts`: try/catch around `unzipSync` (corrupt zip → recorded scan failure, not unhandled crash).
- `scan-bundle.ts`: log VersionStateError catches (still idempotent — log surfaces production triage).

**UX:**
- `new.vue` category/scope `<option>` labels via `t('publish.options.*')`; en+zh have the keys.

**Skipped** (in commit body): `DEFAULT_ORG_ID` (matches locked single-tenant-UI decision), "move under `[locale]/`" (recurring false positive), docstring coverage (CLAUDE.md conflict).

114 tests still passing. Commitlint flagged a footer-leading-blank warning (cosmetic, didn't block the commit). PR #7 should re-run CI on the new push.

{
  "file_path": "/Users/hutusi/workspace/ai/naive/agentcenter-nuxt/docs/deploy.md",
  "content": "# Deployment\n\nAgentCenter (Nuxt) ships as a standalone Node server, with Postgres + an object store + Inngest behind it. Two deploy targets are supported:\n\n- **Node** (default) — `nitro: { preset: \"node-server\" }`. Runs anywhere Node 22+ runs: bare metal, container, PaaS.\n- **Cloudflare** (stretch) — `nitro: { preset: \"cloudflare_module\" }`. Workers + R2 binding. Not maintained alongside primary; expect bundle-size + driver tweaks.\n\nThis guide covers the Node path. The Cloudflare path is a config flip plus a storage driver swap.\n\n## Prerequisites\n\n| Service | Purpose | Required |\n|---|---|---|\n| **PostgreSQL 15+** | Application database | yes |\n| **Object storage** — Supabase Storage **or** Cloudflare R2 | Extension bundles | yes |\n| **Inngest** account (cloud) or local dev server | Background jobs (scan, index) | yes (cloud for prod) |\n| **Node 22+** | Runtime | yes |\n| **Bun 1.3.12** | Build (production runs Node, not Bun) | yes during build |\n\n## 1. Provision the database\n\nAny Postgres works — Supabase, Neon, AWS RDS, self-hosted. Apply migrations:\n\n```bash\nbun install\nDATABASE_URL=\"postgresql://...\" bun run db:migrate\nDATABASE_URL=\"postgresql://...\" bun run db:apply-fts\nDATABASE_URL=\"postgresql://...\" bun run db:seed   # optional: 16 sample extensions\n```\n\nThe `db:apply-fts` step requires `psql` on PATH. It runs `drizzle/0002_fts_search_vector.sql` against your DB (FTS column + trgm indexes).\n\n## 2. Provision object storage\n\n### Supabase Storage (default)\n\n1. Supabase dashboard → Storage → New bucket (e.g. `agentcenter-bundles`)\n2. Generate a service-role key (Settings → API → service_role secret)\n3. Set env: `SUPABASE_URL`, `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY`, `SUPABASE_BUCKET`\n\n### Cloudflare R2 (alternative)\n\n1. Cloudflare dashboard → R2 → Create bucket\n2. Create an API token with Object Read & Write on the bucket\n3. Set env: `R2_ACCOUNT_ID`, `R2_ACCESS_KEY_ID`, `R2_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY`, `R2_BUCKET`\n4. Apply CORS so browsers can `PUT` direct to R2 (the upload-sign endpoint hands out presigned URLs; the browser uploads without proxying through the app)\n\n`R2_ACCOUNT_ID` being set picks R2 over Supabase automatically. See `server/utils/storage.ts`.\n\n## 3. Inngest\n\n1. Create an Inngest app (cloud) and copy `INNGEST_EVENT_KEY` + `INNGEST_SIGNING_KEY`\n2. After deploying, register the webhook URL in the Inngest dashboard:\n   ```\n   https://yourdomain.com/api/inngest\n   ```\n3. Inngest will verify by calling the endpoint; `scan-bundle` and `reindex-search` will appear as registered functions\n\nFor local dev, run the Inngest dev server instead:\n```bash\nbunx inngest-cli@latest dev\n```\nIt auto-discovers `/api/inngest` and routes events locally. No event/signing keys needed locally.\n\n## 4. Build & run\n\n```bash\nbun install --frozen-lockfile\nbun run build\nPORT=3000 node .output/server/index.mjs\n```\n\nFront the Node process with a reverse proxy (nginx, Caddy) for TLS, gzip, and HTTP/2.\n\n### Required env vars at runtime\n\n| Variable | Purpose |\n|---|---|\n| `DATABASE_URL` | Postgres connection string |\n| `BETTER_AUTH_URL` | Public origin (e.g. `https://agentcenter.example.com`) |\n| `BETTER_AUTH_SECRET` | Random 32+ char string (`openssl rand -base64 32`) |\n| `NUXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL` | Public origin (same as `BETTER_AUTH_URL`) |\n| `NODE_ENV=production` | Enables prod cookies, prod Inngest routing, etc. |\n| `INNGEST_EVENT_KEY` | Inngest cloud event key |\n| `INNGEST_SIGNING_KEY` | Inngest cloud webhook verification key |\n| `SUPABASE_URL` + `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY` + `SUPABASE_BUCKET` | Storage (if using Supabase) |\n| `R2_ACCOUNT_ID` + `R2_ACCESS_KEY_ID` + `R2_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY` + `R2_BUCKET` | Storage (if using R2) |\n\nSee `.env.example` for the canonical list.\n\n## 5. Health checks\n\nAfter the server is running:\n\n- `curl https://yourdomain.com/api/v1/extensions` → 200 with `{ items, total, page, pageSize }`\n- `curl -I https://yourdomain.com/` → 302 to `/en`\n- `curl https://yourdomain.com/en/extensions` → 200 with the browse page HTML\n- Sign-up via the UI → land on `/en/onboard` → pick a department → land on `/en/`\n- Publish a test bundle (zip with valid `manifest.toml`) via `/en/publish/new` → scope=personal → Inngest scans → row appears on `/en/extensions`\n- Build the CLI binary from `../agentcenter/cli/`, point at production URL, run `agentcenter login` end-to-end through the device-code flow\n\n## 6. Upgrades\n\nMigrations are idempotent (Drizzle journal-based). For zero-downtime upgrades:\n\n1. Apply new migrations against the live DB before swapping app binaries\n2. Run the FTS migration once (only re-run if `drizzle/0002_fts_search_vector.sql` was changed)\n3. Hot-swap the Node process behind the reverse proxy (PM2, systemd, blue/green)\n\n## 7. Cloudflare deploy (stretch)\n\n```ts\n// nuxt.config.ts\nnitro: { preset: \"cloudflare_module\" }\n```\n\nPlus:\n- Swap `drizzle-orm/postgres-js` (TCP) for `@neondatabase/serverless` (HTTP) or Hyperdrive — Workers can't open raw TCP\n- Use the R2 binding (`event.context.cloudflare.env.BUCKET`) instead of the S3 SDK; cuts bundle size significantly\n- `wrangler secret put` for each runtime env var\n\nBoth swaps are localized to `server/utils/db.ts` and `server/utils/storage.ts`. Everything else is preset-agnostic.\n\nThis path is documented but not maintained alongside the Node path. If you need it, expect a half-day of bundle-size triage on first deploy.\n"
}
```

{
  "file_path": "/Users/hutusi/workspace/ai/naive/agentcenter-nuxt/README.md",
  "content": "# AgentCenter (Nuxt)\n\nA bilingual (EN/ZH) marketplace for AI agent extensions — Skills, MCP servers, slash commands, and plugins. Nuxt 4 rewrite of the original Next.js implementation; same `/api/v1` contract so the existing CLI binary keeps working.\n\n## What's in here\n\n- **Web app** — browse, filter, search, and view extension detail pages; sign up and publish your own extensions; bilingual UI with always-prefixed locales (`/en/...`, `/zh/...`)\n- **Public registry API** — the `/api/v1/...` surface the CLI talks to\n- **Background workers** — Inngest jobs scan uploaded bundles and auto-publish personal-scope extensions\n\n## Tech stack\n\n| Layer | Choice |\n|---|---|\n| Framework | Nuxt 4 (Nitro, Vue 3, Vite) |\n| Language | TypeScript strict (with `noUncheckedIndexedAccess`, `exactOptionalPropertyTypes`, `noImplicitOverride`) |\n| Styling | Tailwind v4 |\n| Runtime | Node 22+ (production); Bun 1.3.12 (build + scripts) |\n| Database | PostgreSQL via Drizzle ORM (`drizzle-orm/postgres-js`) |\n| Auth | Better Auth (cookie sessions; CLI device-code flow on the same `sessions` table) |\n| Storage | Supabase Storage (default) or Cloudflare R2 |\n| Background jobs | Inngest |\n| i18n | `@nuxtjs/i18n` with `strategy: \"prefix\"`, locales `en` (default) + `zh` |\n| Search | Postgres FTS + `pg_trgm` |\n| Tests | Vitest (unit + component via `@nuxt/test-utils`) + Playwright (E2E) |\n\n## Quickstart\n\n```bash\n# 1. Install dependencies\nbun install\n\n# 2. Provision a Postgres + copy the URL\ncp .env.example .env   # then fill in DATABASE_URL etc.\n\n# 3. Migrations + sample data\nbun run db:migrate\nbun run db:apply-fts\nbun run db:seed\n\n# 4. Dev server\nbun run dev\n```\n\nOpen <http://localhost:3000>. The minimum env vars needed for local browsing are `DATABASE_URL`, `BETTER_AUTH_URL`, `BETTER_AUTH_SECRET`. Add storage + Inngest for the publish flow. See [`docs/deploy.md`](./docs/deploy.md).\n\n## Scripts\n\n| Command | What it does |\n|---|---|\n| `bun run dev` | Dev server (Nitro + Vite) |\n| `bun run build` | Production build → `.output/` |\n| `bun run preview` | Run the production build locally |\n| `bun run prepare` | Husky + `nuxt prepare` (type generation) |\n| `bun run lint` | `@nuxt/eslint` |\n| `bun run typecheck` | `nuxi typecheck` (vue-tsc) |\n| `bun run test` | Vitest unit + component tests |\n| `bun run test:coverage` | Vitest with v8 coverage |\n| `bun run test:e2e` | Playwright E2E (needs dev server + seeded DB) |\n| `bun run validate` | `prepare → lint → typecheck → test` — mirrors CI |\n| `bun run db:migrate` | Apply Drizzle migrations |\n| `bun run db:apply-fts` | Apply the FTS migration (requires `psql`) |\n| `bun run db:seed` | Seed sample extensions, tags, departments |\n| `bun run db:studio` | Drizzle Studio |\n\n## Documentation\n\n- [`docs/plan.md`](./docs/plan.md) — full implementation plan\n- [`docs/deploy.md`](./docs/deploy.md) — deployment runbook\n- [`docs/api.md`](./docs/api.md) — public `/api/v1/...` contract\n- [`CONTRIBUTING.md`](./CONTRIBUTING.md) — workflow, commits, PRs\n- [`CLAUDE.md`](./CLAUDE.md) — project rules and locked decisions\n\n## Workflow\n\nAll changes go through a feature branch and a pull request. `bun run validate` mirrors what CI runs on every PR (lint, typecheck, tests). See [`CONTRIBUTING.md`](./CONTRIBUTING.md) for details.\n"
}
```

Surfaces status code but never raw error messages (Drizzle's \\`NeonDbError\\` leaks SQL fragments).\n  - \\`<NuxtLoadingIndicator>\\` in \\`app.vue\\` — thin progress bar during route transitions, tied to \\`--color-accent\\` so it adapts to ivory/dark.\n  - \\`errors.generic.*\\` + \\`extensions.errorBoundary.*\\` i18n keys (en + zh).\n\n- **P14 — Deploy runbook + env template + README**:\n  - \\`docs/deploy.md\\` — eight-section Node runbook (DB provision → storage → Inngest → build/run → env vars → health checks → upgrades → Cloudflare stretch notes).\n  - \\`.env.example\\` — cleaned wording, pick-one storage block, Inngest dev note.\n  - \\`README.md\\` — repo-level intro: tech stack table, quickstart, scripts table, doc index. Mirrors the original Next.js repo's README structure with Nuxt-specific changes.\n\n## Why\n\nPR #6 closed the publish loop. This PR makes the app production-deployable: an operator can clone the repo, follow \\`docs/deploy.md\\`, and have a working marketplace. Without the error boundary, any DB hiccup shows Nuxt's default error page; with it, users see a friendly retry CTA in the app shell.\n\n## Test plan\n\n- [x] \\`bun run validate\\` exits 0 (114 tests still passing)\n- [x] CI green expected\n- [ ] **Reviewer with local Postgres**:\n  - Throw inside an endpoint (or kill the DB mid-request) → see the new error page with topbar/sidebar intact + a \"Back to home\" CTA + status code chip\n  - Navigate between pages → see the loading bar flash at the top of the viewport in the accent color\n  - Read \\`docs/deploy.md\\` straight through — does any step assume context the file doesn't provide?\n\n## Tradeoffs\n\n- **No per-route \\`<NuxtErrorBoundary>\\` wrappers.** The global \\`app/error.vue\\` covers every uncaught throw. Per-route boundaries (extensions list, detail) are a defensive nicety; the i18n keys are pre-positioned so adding them later is mechanical.\n- **No OG images.** The original plan listed \\`@nuxtjs/og-image\\` as a P13 deliverable. Deferred — share-link previews are a nice-to-have, not load-bearing, and the package adds ~2MB of dev deps + a build-time step. Add later if/when social-sharing matters.\n- **No exhaustive a11y/dark-mode sweep.** The components use CSS variables that adapt cleanly to both themes; focus rings exist on every interactive element; skip-link from P1 still works. A real Lighthouse pass with screen-reader testing is a separate effort that can land outside the rewrite.\n- **No status polling on the publisher dashboard.** A scan that takes >10s leaves the user re-loading manually.
